experimentos_incluidos: PSI-181: Pb-Sn and Sn-Ag-Cu solders in microgravity and extreme temperatures (ISSI)
ISSI Lunar/Mars (PSI-181): soldering, electronic repair and the cryogenic lunar night
modificaciones_necesarias: [Apollo 13]: 1) Add a third O2 tank isolated in another compartment; 2) Upgrade thermostats to withstand 65 V DC; 3) Remove mechanical stirring fans inside O2 tanks; 4) Encase wiring in stainless-steel sheathing; 5) Reform detanking test procedures and manufacturing change control.

[Apollo 1]: 1) Redesign a unified quick-opening hatch (opens outward in 3 s from inside or outside); 2) Replace the 100% O2 launch atmosphere with a 60% O2 / 40% N2 mix on the pad; 3) Strictly restrict and relocate combustible materials (Velcro, nylon) and adopt Beta cloth fabrics / fire-resistant suits; 4) Shield wiring and plumbing to the Block II standard; 5) Mandatory hazardous-test protocols with on-site rescue.

[PSI-181: Pb-Sn and Sn-Ag-Cu solders in microgravity and extreme temperatures (ISSI)]: 1) Use solder wire without a volatile flux core, or apply vacuum/ultrasonic degassing during in-orbit electronic repairs (in-space manufacturing/repair), to avoid trapped pores that create hot spots and electrical ignition; 2) Prefer doped SAC formulations with intermetallic control for lunar missions with cryogenic cycling.

[ISSI Lunar/Mars (PSI-181): soldering, electronic repair and the cryogenic lunar night]: 1) Require vacuum-assisted reflow or fluxless ultrasonic soldering for all electronic repairs on the Moon and Mars; 2) Derate by 25% the maximum current of traces and solder joints operating in 34% O2 exploration atmospheres.
[Li-ion batteries (NESC / Gateway HALO)]: Enforce strict state-of-charge limits in transit, FTRC thermal isolation between cells, HALO containment bags and dedicated ECLSS catalysts for HF/POF3.

experimentos_incluidos: PSI-108: STDCE-1 (Surface Tension Driven Convection Experiment - 1)
PSI-117: Multiphysics CFD dynamics of cool flames under thermoconvective perturbation
PSI-142: Cool-flame transitions in radiative and strain extinction
PSI-159: ACME / CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases)
FLEX & CFI partial-g: cool flames and fuel droplets on the Moon and Mars
modificaciones_necesarias: [FLEX]: 1) Raise the minimum concentrations of inert suppressant gases (N2, CO2, He) above terrestrial standards; 2) Add infrared/spectral sensors to detect invisible cool flames and keep post-extinction monitoring to prevent spontaneous reignition.
[FLEX-2]: 1) Update engine and thruster kinetic models with slow radiative and convective droplet-droplet coupling; 2) Adjust injection spacing in droplet arrays to mitigate soot and reignition.

[Cool Flames (iniciativa)]: 1) Update post-fire procedures on the ISS/Artemis to require full cooling and controlled venting of partially oxidized vapours (formaldehyde/CO) before reopening compartments where a flame seemed to go out.
[Cool flames]: Add mid-wave IR cameras and CO/formaldehyde sensors to verify complete chemical (not just visual) extinction after a fire.

[PSI-68: FLEX-2 (Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2)]: 1) Integrate low-temperature kinetic sub-mechanisms (NTC / RO2 alkyl peroxides) into space propulsion and safety CFD models to predict cool flames (550-750 K); 2) Install UV (OH* at 310 nm) + UV/visible (HCHO* at 395 nm) and IR optical diagnostics in combustion chambers and habitats; 3) Raise the CO2/N2 dilution margin by at least +4% to suppress both the hot-flame and cool-flame branches in heavy hydrocarbons.

[PSI-69: FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment)]: 1) Raise the design concentration of inert agents (N2, CO2) by +3 to +5% relative to terrestrial NFPA standards; 2) Add spectral monitoring of excited formaldehyde (HCHO*) and mid-infrared after any apparent extinction of liquid hydrocarbons.

[PSI-39: CFI (Cool Flames Investigation)]: 1) Differentiate in-orbit safety and suppression protocols by the liquid's molecular structure (linear alkanes with a high risk of invisible cool flames vs esters/alcohols without an NTC branch).

[PSI-108: STDCE-1 (Surface Tension Driven Convection Experiment - 1)]: 1) Include Marangoni thermocapillary shear-stress boundary conditions (d_sigma/dT) in flame-spread models over liquids and molten polymer pools in microgravity.

[PSI-117: Multiphysics CFD dynamics of cool flames under thermoconvective perturbation]: 1) Avoid sudden ventilation pulses over post-extinction hydrocarbon vapour clouds, since the convective wake concentrates RO2/H2O2 radicals and triggers secondary hot reignition.

[PSI-142: Cool-flame transitions in radiative and strain extinction]: 1) Update strain-extinction criteria (critical Damköhler number) in space engines and suppression systems using the 4-branch S-curve that includes the cool-flame regime.

[PSI-159: ACME / CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases)]: 1) Extend cool-flame detection protocols (HCHO* and CO sensors) to leaks of light gaseous hydrocarbons (propane, butane, pentane) in space thermal and propulsion systems.

[FLEX & CFI partial-g: cool flames and fuel droplets on the Moon and Mars]: 1) In lunar/Martian solvent stores, laboratories and greenhouses, keep forced extraction >25 cm/s or inert with CO2/N2 after any liquid incident to prevent reignition by a cool-flame buoyant plume.

experimentos_incluidos: PSI-21: ACME / CLD Flame (Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame)
PSI-22: ACME / E-FIELD Flames (Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames)
PSI-23: ACME / s-Flame (Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames)
PSI-60: Computational and experimental analysis of SPICE data
PSI-106: SLICE (Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment)
PSI-107: SPICE (Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment)
ACME E-FIELD Lunar/Mars: emulating partial gravity with ionic wind
modificaciones_necesarias: [SPICE]: 1) Recalibrate smoke-point thresholds in buoyancy-free laminar burners; 2) Keep fuel flow below the soot-release threshold to avoid radiative losses and filter clogging on the ISS.
[SLICE]: 1) Adjust coflow velocity and nozzle geometry to stabilize lifted flames without blow-off; 2) Integrate the high-resolution optical diagnostics later implemented in ACME CLD Flame.
[LSP]: 1) Include long-residence-time soot radiation in CFD combustion models; 2) Tune cabin optical detectors and filters for primary soot aggregates larger than in 1 g.
[TGDF]: 1) Remove buoyancy turbulent-production terms from k-epsilon / LES models for microgravity; 2) Redesign jet injectors for the longer turbulent flame length in 0 g.
[ELF]: 1) Evolve the confined wind tunnel into the modular SPICE/SLICE architecture in the MSG; 2) Control the duct-wall boundary layer to avoid disturbing the flame base.
[CLD Flame]: 1) Extend detailed chemical mechanisms for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) precursors and soot to high N2-dilution regimes.

[E-FIELD Flames]: 1) Install high-voltage electrode meshes (up to 10 kV) to induce forced convection by ionic wind, reducing soot formation and allowing lunar/Martian gravity (0.16 g - 0.38 g) to be emulated.
[Flame Design]: 1) Reconfigure burner stoichiometry (shifting the oxidizer or diluent) to run in O2-enriched atmospheres with strong flames free of soot and excess radiation.
[s-Flame]: 1) Include gas radiative losses (CO2, H2O) and Lewis-number coupling in extinction models of large spherical flames in space habitats.

[PSI-10: ACME / Flame Design]: 1) Reconfigure space burners and incinerators by moving the diluent (N2/CO2) into the fuel stream to raise Z_st > 0.35, eliminating soot and excess thermal radiation even in O2-enriched exploration atmospheres.

[PSI-21: ACME / CLD Flame (Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame)]: 1) Recalibrate the edge/triple-flame stabilization and soot-radiation sub-models in CFD codes for low-emission combustors and space burners.

[PSI-22: ACME / E-FIELD Flames (Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames)]: 1) Add high-voltage electrode rings/meshes (6-9 kV, < 1 W) to orbital burners and incinerators to replace mechanical fans with ionic-wind convection and eliminate soot emission.

[PSI-23: ACME / s-Flame (Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames)]: 1) Include pulsating diffusive-thermal instability criteria (Le > 1) and CO2/H2O radiative reabsorption in spherical fire spread and extinction models for space cabins.

[PSI-60: Computational and experimental analysis of SPICE data]: 1) Couple optically thin/thick radiation models with OH- and O2-radical soot oxidation kinetics to predict sudden soot release (wing/tip opening) in space fires.

[PSI-106: SLICE (Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment)]: 1) Design flame holders in space combustion systems taking into account that liftoff height in 0 g is more sensitive to the coflow momentum deficit.

[PSI-107: SPICE (Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment)]: 1) Apply a 3x safety reduction factor to terrestrial smoke-point tables (ASTM D1322) when assessing soot propensity and HEPA filter loading in space fires.

[ACME E-FIELD Lunar/Mars: emulating partial gravity with ionic wind]: 1) Use the PSI-22 (E-FIELD) voltage-gravity correlation to qualify burners, regolith-processing torches and methane leak sensors (CH4/LOX) for lunar and Martian missions.

experimentos_incluidos: PSI-25: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids - II)
PSI-26: BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids)
PSI-62: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling (FGM & Two-Color Tomography)
LUCI & FM2: flammability at lunar gravity (0.16 g) and the U-shaped LOI curve
modificaciones_necesarias: [BRE]: 1) Calibrate the feedback between surface thermocouples, radiant heat-flux sensors and the gas mass-flow valve to emulate the mass-transfer B-number of real polymers in space habitats.

[BASS]: 1) Revise NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (upward burning in 1 g) because it underestimates flammability in microgravity at low flows (~1-10 cm/s); 2) Prohibit applying slow localized N2 jets directly at the flame base without first cutting HVAC ventilation, since entrained O2 intensifies the fire.
[Flammability limit]: Lower the maximum allowed oxygen threshold (MOC) in space-material certification tables by an extra 2-4% O2 relative to 1 g ground tests.
[NASA standard test]: Replace or complement NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 with slow opposed-flow tests and a Narrow Channel apparatus calibrated with BASS and SoFIE data.
[Spread direction]: Reverse the geometry of firebreak barriers and the placement of thermal sensors in ducts/racks so they also watch upstream (toward the ventilation air inlet).
[Spacecraft ventilation]: Automate an immediate HVAC ventilation shutoff (flow to 0 cm/s) on detecting smoke or flame radiation, before discharging the extinguishing agent.
[Localized suppression]: Redesign extinguisher nozzles with total-flooding diffusers or enveloping mist instead of narrow inert-gas jets that induce O2 mixing.

[PSI-25: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids - II)]: 1) Lower the MOC certification threshold for cabin polymers and textiles to <= 15.0% O2 for slow-ventilation regimes (0.5-8 cm/s); 2) Add two-branch extinction curves (radiative quenching < 1 cm/s and convective blowoff > 30 cm/s) to the Orion/Gateway fire code; 3) Require a waiting time after ventilation shutoff (> 60 s) because of the thermal inertia of thick solids (PMMA >= 3.2 mm).

[PSI-26: BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids)]: 1) Prohibit narrow N2-jet extinguisher nozzles without first cutting ventilation; 2) Reorient thermal sensors upstream of electronic components; 3) Replace the one-dimensional criterion of NASA-STD-6001 Test 1.

[PSI-62: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling (FGM & Two-Color Tomography)]: 1) Adopt pre-integrated Unsteady Flamelet Generated Manifold (UFGM) tables with non-adiabatic radiative losses in cabin-certification CFD codes; 2) Calibrate soot-emission models with volume-fraction profiles measured by two-color optical tomography.

[PSI-20: ACME / BRE (Burning Rate Emulator)]: 1) Use the BRE parameter matrix (heat of gasification L_g and B-number) to pre-screen candidate cabin polymers without burning hundreds of solid samples in orbit.

[LUCI & FM2: flammability at lunar gravity (0.16 g) and the U-shaped LOI curve]: 1) Replace terrestrial NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (1 g) certification with tests or correction factors at the minimum of the U-shaped LOI curve (equivalent flow of 6.5-8.0 cm/s for lunar 0.16 g); 2) Build into the prediction engine the intrinsic buoyant velocity V_eff = sqrt(V_forced^2 + V_buoyant(g)^2) and de Ris scaling (V_f ~ (k*rho*c)^(-1) for thin solids).

experimentos_incluidos: PSI-98: SAFFIRE-I (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - I)
PSI-99: SAFFIRE-II (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - II)
PSI-100: SAFFIRE-III (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - III)
SAFFIRE IV-VI & SoFIE SEA: Lunar/Martian atmospheres (8.2 psia / 34% O2)
MARS-0.38g & CO2-ISRU: combustion at Martian gravity and CO2 diluent
SoFIE (ISS CIR - GEL, MIST, SMuRF, RTDFS, NCA)
modificaciones_necesarias: [SoFIE]: 1) Certify all cabin polymers (PMMA, Delrin, fabrics) under low-pressure, high-O2 exploration atmospheres (up to 40% O2 and 0.2-1.5 atm) with real HVAC ventilation flows (0-30 cm/s).

[SoFIE: Flammability correlation]: 1) Replace the single pass/fail criterion of NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 with multidimensional maps of the maximum oxygen concentration (MOC) as a function of forced-flow velocity and pressure.
[SoFIE: Growth and extinction]: 1) Include the solid's internal preheating and surface curvature in predictive radiative-extinction models.
[SoFIE: Thermal and species fields]: 1) Set minimum safe thicknesses for cabin coatings and plastic films below the thermal/species spread threshold.

[SoFIE: External heat flux]: 1) Cut the maximum allowed radiant heat flux near electronics and cables in spacecraft by 50% relative to the terrestrial standard; 2) Increase thermal insulation in power racks.

[SoFIE: Narrow Channel]: 1) Adopt the Narrow Channel Apparatus in ground laboratories as a standard complementary method to, or replacement for, NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 to pre-certify space materials in 1 g.
[Ignition]: Halve the maximum allowed temperature/heat flux on surfaces near cables and batteries; reinforce fast-acting circuit breakers.

[PSI-98: SAFFIRE-I (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - I)]: 1) Update cabin emergency-response models with the large-scale steady spread rate and the fast pressure/temperature rise in a closed volume; 2) Validate that cutting ventilation immediately stops a 0.4 m-wide flame front.

[PSI-99: SAFFIRE-II (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - II)]: 1) Penalize in certification protocols geometries with exposed edges, grooves or ribs in thick polymers (PMMA/polycarbonate), since they sustain the flame when the flat surface does not burn; 2) Restrict silicone membranes thinner than 1.5 mm in ducts with flow >= 20 cm/s.

[PSI-100: SAFFIRE-III (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - III)]: 1) Limit the maximum air velocity in space-habitat corridors and plenums to < 15 cm/s; 2) Size post-fire pressure relief and CO/CO2 scrubbing systems for heat release rates that scale linearly with ventilation velocity.

[SAFFIRE IV-VI & SoFIE SEA: Lunar/Martian atmospheres (8.2 psia / 34% O2)]: 1) Prohibit materials certified only at 21% O2 inside modules pressurized to 8.2 psia / 34% O2 (HLS, Gateway, lunar/Martian rovers); 2) Install far-field catalytic scrubbers (Far-Field Scrubbers for CO, CO2, HCl and HF tested in SAFFIRE IV-VI) and a rapid post-fire depressurization/repressurization protocol.

[MARS-0.38g & CO2-ISRU: combustion at Martian gravity and CO2 diluent]: 1) Use purified, compressed Martian atmospheric CO2 as the primary flooding and inerting fire system in Martian habitats; 2) Physically isolate solid-oxide electrolysis ISRU plants (MOXIE type, 800 °C, high-purity O2) outside the pressurized habitable volume.
[SoFIE (ISS CIR - GEL, MIST, SMuRF, RTDFS, NCA)]: Make the 5 SoFIE sub-projects a mandatory calibration reference for SEA atmospheres (34-37% O2) and radiative safety factors.

experimentos_incluidos: PSI-101: SAME-R (Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight)
PSI-47: DAFT / DAFT-2 (Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test)
PSI-115: Advanced modelling of smoke generation (SAME data)
SAME/DAFT Lunar & Mars dust: telling regolith dust from smoke
modificaciones_necesarias: [SAME]: 1) Redesign the laser-scattering optical chambers and threshold algorithms of space smoke detectors (Orion/Gateway/Lunar Lander) to detect the larger particle distributions produced by slow pyrolysis in 0 g.
[DAFT]: 1) Add multi-wavelength discriminating filtering and lunar/ambient dust rejection to fire sensors to avoid false alarms from suspended dust after EVAs.
[Smoke detection]: Recalibrate optical scattering angles and detection algorithms for the large agglomerated particles typical of microgravity.

[PSI-101: SAME-R (Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight)]: 1) Replace ionization smoke detectors (designed for ultrafine particles < 0.1 microns in 1 g) with laser-scattering photoelectric detectors calibrated for the 0.3-1.5 micron range measured in SAME-R; 2) Include coagulation-compensation algorithms for slow transport through the cabin.

[PSI-102: SAME (Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment)]: 1) Deploy dual-wavelength (blue + near-infrared) smoke sensors that measure the size-moment ratio (mean diameter) at the same time, to tell Teflon/wire pyrolysis (small particles) from silicone/cellulose smoke or ambient dust.

[PSI-47: DAFT / DAFT-2 (Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test)]: 1) Exploit the low cabin background of ultrafine particles (thanks to HEPA filtering) by setting early pre-alarm thresholds on condensation-nucleus counts (CPC) for incipient electrical overloads; 2) Temporarily mask the pre-alarm in the food-warmer (galley) area.

[PSI-115: Advanced modelling of smoke generation (SAME data)]: 1) Integrate the aerosol population-balance module (PBM with fractal dimension 1.8) into habitat ventilation simulation software (Orion/Gateway) to optimize the placement of photoelectric detectors.

[SAME/DAFT Lunar & Mars dust: telling regolith dust from smoke]: 1) Require multi-criteria smoke detectors (two-wavelength laser scattering + optical depolarization + electrochemical CO cell) in all EVA airlocks and lunar/Martian cabins; 2) Enable a dust false-alarm suppression mode synchronized with airlock pressurization without disabling the CO/pyrolysis channel.
[NASA-STD-6001B & JSC 20584 SMAC / NASA-STD-3001]: Require T_grp < 1 verification after suppression, HEPA filtration <= 0.1 mg/m3 and HF/HCl acid-gas monitoring in Artemis and Mars habitats.

experimentos_incluidos: SCWM Lunar/Mars: fine water mist and hybrid CO2 suppression at 0.16 g/0.38 g
modificaciones_necesarias: [Mist]: 1) Replace CO2 and Halon 1301 extinguishers with fine water-mist extinguishers (Water Mist PFE, droplets < 50 microns), removing the CO2 toxicity risk in a closed cabin.
[SCWM]: 1) Redesign walls and flow in life-support (ECLSS) SCWO reactors to avoid clogging and corrosion from inorganic salt (Na2SO4) precipitation without gravitational settling.
[Water suppression]: Standardize water-mist extinguishers in orbital modules to avoid a lethal CO2 build-up after a discharge.

[SCWM Lunar/Mars: fine water mist and hybrid CO2 suppression at 0.16 g/0.38 g]: 1) Standardize hybrid fine water mist (D32 < 25 microns) + inert gas (N2 on the Moon, in-situ CO2 on Mars) extinguishers for surface habitats at 56.5-70.3 kPa.

[SOFBALL]: 1) Lower the design lower flammability limit (LFL) for hydrogen and light-gas (low Lewis number) leaks in space habitats, since they can sustain stationary ~1 W flame balls below the terrestrial limit.

[Candle Flames]: 1) Drop the assumption that turning off ventilation immediately self-extinguishes a fire in quiescent air; 2) Keep thermal/UV monitoring for faint blue hemispherical flames that persist by pure diffusion.
[Misconceptions]: Update all crew training manuals and aerospace engineering standards to remove the 3 false assumptions.

PSI166_ZrNi_ICOPROSOL_QUASI.categoria_principal: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
modificaciones_necesarias: [PSI-166: Zr64Ni36 (ICOPROSOL / QUASI)]: 1) Switch from the laminar model to the RNG k-epsilon turbulent model above 1460 K (Cycle 29) and 1720 K (Cycle 26); 2) Recalculate the target shear-strain rate for the real slow cooling rates (0.02-1.33 °C/s) so that concentration profiles around subcritical nuclei do not interact; 3) Turn off the heater control voltage (0.000 V) during the free-cooling phase.

PSI166_CuZr_THERMOLAB_PARSEC.categoria_principal: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
modificaciones_necesarias: [PSI-166: Cu50Zr50 (THERMOLAB / PARSEC)]: 1) Review and recalculate the shear-strain-rate target specific to Cu50Zr50 at low cooling rates (0.31-2.01 K/s), considering its own chemical and thermodynamic driving forces; 2) Prefer the low positioner-voltage setup (1.498 V, Cycles 9-10) to minimize pole-equator asymmetry (2.7x vs 24x in Cycles 3-4).

PSI166_TiZrNi_Quasicrystals_ICOPROSOL.categoria_principal: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
modificaciones_necesarias: [PSI-166: Ti39.5Zr39.5Ni21 (ICOPROSOL)]: 1) Recalculate the SRD shear-strain-rate targets separately for the fast-cooling (Cycles 64-66, ~28 K/s) and slow-cooling cycles (Cycles 11, 49, 50, 53, 55, 62, ~2-8 K/s); 2) Lower the positioner voltage in Cycles 65-66 (from 9.39 V to <= 3.87 V) to bring the shear rate down toward the diffusion-controlled regime (0.05-0.5 1/s).

PSI166_Ge_Vit106_AlNi_THERMOLAB.categoria_principal: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
modificaciones_necesarias: [PSI-166: Germanio Dopado (SEMITHERM / THERMOLAB)]: 1) Modify the oscillating-drop damping equation to include turbulent eddy viscosity (from the RNG k-epsilon model) so turbulent damping is discounted; 2) Drastically reduce positioning and heating currents for highly conductive semiconductor samples (1.52e6 S/m).

[PSI-166: Vit106 Bulk Metallic Glass (THERMOLAB)]: 1) Replace the VFT viscosity law with the KKZNT formulation using a Heaviside step function at low temperatures (T < T* = 1471.7 K) to ensure numerical stability in ANSYS Fluent; 2) Recalculate the shear-strain-rate target for each cycle's cooling rate (0.85 to 19.63 °C/s).

[PSI-166: Al75Ni25 and transient pulses (PARSEC)]: 1) Couple transient MHD simulations (RampUp, HoldPos, Pulse, RampDown using UDFs and fidapbdy files) to quantify the hydrodynamic decay time after the excitation pulse before measuring properties or inducing solidification.

Al75Ni25.primary_modification_required: Alto campo EM de bobina calentadora (7.75 V) domina las fuerzas e induce turbulencia intensa; usar modelo turbulento RNG k-epsilon antes de apagar calentador.

Cu50Zr50.primary_modification_required: Flujo laminar con tasa de corte > 5.0 1/s o tasa de enfriamiento distinta a 10 K/s del SRD; recalcular umbral crítico de shear-strain rate según la tasa de enfriamiento real para evitar interacción de perfiles de difusión entre clústeres subcríticos.

Ge.primary_modification_required: Activar modelo de turbulencia RNG k-epsilon (Re >= 250-600 o calentador activo en enfriamiento); corregir amortiguamiento turbulento en mediciones de viscosidad por gota oscilante y reducir corriente de bobinas.

Ti39.5Zr39.5Ni21.primary_modification_required: Tasa de enfriamiento real (2.38 K/s) mucho menor que los 10 K/s del SRD y shear-strain pico ecuatorial (5.74 1/s > 5.0 1/s) superior al límite estricto de clústeres subcríticos; recalcular objetivo de corte en SRD.

Vit106.sub_investigation: ISS-EML / THERMOLAB Bulk Metallic Glass (USTIP Batch 2)
Vit106.primary_modification_required: Reemplazar ajuste VFT (inestable a baja T) por modelo de viscosidad KKZNT; flujo ultra-laminar (shear 0.031 1/s <= 0.05 1/s), revalidar objetivo de corte para enfriamiento de 1.41 K/s.

Zr64Ni36.primary_modification_required: Flujo laminar con tasa de corte > 5.0 1/s o tasa de enfriamiento distinta a 10 K/s del SRD; recalcular umbral crítico de shear-strain rate según la tasa de enfriamiento real para evitar interacción de perfiles de difusión entre clústeres subcríticos.

class_modifications.Laminar_Subcritical_Diffusion_Safe: Diffusion-controlled laminar regime (Re < 250, shear-strain <= 5.0 1/s, within SRD specification); revalidate only the cycle's effective cooling rate and keep a low positioner voltage.
class_modifications.Laminar_Shear_Recalculate_SRD: Laminar flow with shear rate > 5.0 1/s or a cooling rate other than the SRD's 10 K/s; recalculate the critical shear-strain-rate threshold for the real cooling rate to avoid interaction of diffusion profiles between subcritical clusters.
class_modifications.Turbulent_RNG_k_epsilon_Damping_Fix: Enable the RNG k-epsilon turbulence model (Re >= 250-600 or heater active during cooling); correct turbulent damping in oscillating-drop viscosity measurements and reduce coil current.

entries.experimento_investigacion: Apollo 1 (AS-204, CM-012)
entries.categoria: Spacecraft accident
entries.investigador_responsable: NASA SMA / Apollo 204 Review Board
entries.material_combustible: Combustible materials inside the cabin (nylon, Velcro, foam); pure oxygen atmosphere
entries.condiciones: Cabin pressurized with 100% oxygen (16.7 psi), hatches closed, suits on; three-piece hatch that took ~90 s to open under ideal conditions
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Sudden fire in the command module during an internal-power test (Plugs-Out Test); evidence of electrical arcing in vulnerable wiring near the environmental control system

entries.material_combustible: Fuel blends, real-fuel surrogates, biofuels
entries.condiciones: Slow convective flow effects, droplet-droplet interaction, droplet arrays
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Study soot formation, fuel range and flame spread across droplet arrays
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Basis for studying combustion of practical liquid fuels and flame spread between neighbouring droplets
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Update engine and thruster kinetic models with slow radiative and convective droplet-droplet coupling; 2) Adjust injection spacing in droplet arrays to mitigate soot and reignition.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: SPICE - Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment
entries.categoria: Gaseous diffusion flames
entries.investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban (NASA GRC)
entries.material_combustible: Gaseous fuels in coflow
entries.condiciones: Axisymmetric laminar flame
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Transition from soot-free to sooting flame (smoke point)
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: The smoke point indicates a fuel's tendency to produce soot and thermal radiation in microgravity
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Recalibrate smoke-point thresholds in buoyancy-free laminar burners; 2) Keep fuel flow below the soot-release threshold to avoid radiative losses and filter clogging on the ISS.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: SLICE - Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
entries.categoria: Gaseous diffusion flames
entries.investigador_responsable: M. B. Long (Yale)
entries.material_combustible: Combustibles gaseosos
entries.condiciones: Lifted flames at different coflow rates
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Structure of lifted flames; improve efficiency and reduce pollutants
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Precursor of CLD Flame; characterizes stabilization of a flame base detached from the nozzle
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Adjust coflow velocity and nozzle geometry to stabilize lifted flames without blow-off; 2) Integrate the high-resolution optical diagnostics later implemented in ACME CLD Flame.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: LSP - Laminar Soot Processes
entries.categoria: Gaseous diffusion flames
entries.investigador_responsable: G. Faeth (U. Michigan)
entries.material_combustible: Gases (etileno, propano)
entries.condiciones: Sealed chamber, quiescent environment
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Soot formation and oxidation in quiescent diffusion flames
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Reference data for soot formation/destruction models without buoyant acceleration
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Include long-residence-time soot radiation in CFD combustion models; 2) Tune cabin optical detectors and filters for primary soot aggregates larger than in 1 g.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: TGDF - Turbulent Gas-jet Diffusion Flame
entries.categoria: Gaseous diffusion flames
entries.investigador_responsable: M. Y. Bahadori (SAIC)
entries.material_combustible: Propane/hydrogen gas
entries.condiciones: Sealed chamber; iris that induces vortices in the air
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Flame-vortex interaction and stability in turbulent jets
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Improves understanding of momentum-dominated turbulent combustion without buoyancy
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Remove buoyancy turbulent-production terms from k-epsilon / LES models for microgravity; 2) Redesign jet injectors for the longer turbulent flame length in 0 g.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: ELF - Enclosed Laminar Flames
entries.categoria: Gaseous diffusion flames
entries.investigador_responsable: L. D. Chen (U. Iowa)
entries.material_combustible: Gas metano/propano
entries.condiciones: Duct with fan (forced coflow)
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Stability of a laminar flame confined in a duct
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: SLICE is its second generation; it showed the role of confinement and coflow in liftoff height
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Evolve the confined wind tunnel into the modular SPICE/SLICE architecture in the MSG; 2) Control the duct-wall boundary layer to avoid disturbing the flame base.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: BRE - Burning Rate Emulator (ACME)
entries.categoria: Flammable material / fire prevention
entries.investigador_responsable: J. G. Quintiere (U. Maryland)
entries.material_combustible: Flat porous burner with gaseous fuel that mimics paper, plastic and alcohol
entries.condiciones: Fuel flow controlled by heat flux and surface temperature
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Understand ignition and extinction of materials and evaluate flammability tests in low gravity
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Focused on spacecraft fire prevention by emulating the heat of vaporization of solids with gas
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Calibrate the feedback between surface thermocouples, radiant heat-flux sensors and the gas mass-flow valve to emulate the mass-transfer B-number of real polymers in space habitats.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: CLD Flame - Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (ACME)
entries.categoria: Gaseous diffusion flames
entries.investigador_responsable: M. B. Long (Yale)
entries.material_combustible: Methane and ethylene diluted in air coflow
entries.condiciones: Highly diluted and highly sooting flames; lifted flames
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Verify kinetic and soot models at dilution extremes
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Applicable to ignition limits and flame stability in extreme regimes
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Extend detailed chemical mechanisms for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) precursors and soot to high N2-dilution regimes.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: E-FIELD Flames - Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (ACME)
entries.categoria: Gaseous diffusion flames
entries.investigador_responsable: D. Dunn-Rankin (UC Irvine)
entries.material_combustible: Coflow or simple jet flame (methane/ethylene)
entries.condiciones: Electric field up to 10 kV
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Use ions to control diffusion flames through ionic wind
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Measure ion current and flame response; makes it possible to emulate convection equivalent to partial gravity without thermal buoyancy
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Install high-voltage electrode meshes (up to 10 kV) to induce forced convection by ionic wind, reducing soot formation and allowing lunar/Martian gravity (0.16 g - 0.38 g) to be emulated.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Flame Design - Flame Design (ACME)
entries.categoria: Gaseous diffusion flames
entries.investigador_responsable: R. L. Axelbaum (Washington U.)
entries.material_combustible: Ethylene or methane in an O2-enriched atmosphere
entries.condiciones: Spherical flames; possible inverse spherical flame if safety approves
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Soot inception and design of robust soot-free flames
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Determination of soot and flammability limits by controlling the stoichiometric structure
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Reconfigure burner stoichiometry (shifting the oxidizer or diluent) to run in O2-enriched atmospheres with strong flames free of soot and excess radiation.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: s-Flame - Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (ACME)
entries.categoria: Gaseous diffusion flames
entries.investigador_responsable: C. K. Law (Princeton)
entries.material_combustible: Hydrogen and methane (soot-free); ethylene (sooting)
entries.condiciones: Spherical porous burner; various diluents
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Radiative and convective extinction limits; pulsating instabilities
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: A one-dimensional spherical flame, possible only in microgravity; reveals pulsating instabilities before radiative extinction
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Include gas radiative losses (CO2, H2O) and Lewis-number coupling in extinction models of large spherical flames in space habitats.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: BASS - Burning and Suppression of Solids
entries.categoria: Solids / material flammability
entries.investigador_responsable: S. L. Olson / P. Ferkul (NASA GRC)
entries.material_combustible: Flat samples, PMMA spheres, porous wax sheets, wax candles, cotton/fiberglass fabrics
entries.condiciones: Nominal air 21% O2, 1 atm; tests down to 17% O2; variable flow (0-35 cm/s); nitrogen suppression
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Burning and extinction of solids; improve 1 g safety tests and extinction strategies
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative; materials burn at lower O2 in microgravity; a local nitrogen jet can strengthen the flame
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Revise NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (upward burning in 1 g) because it underestimates flammability in microgravity at low flows (~1-10 cm/s); 2) Prohibit applying slow localized N2 jets directly at the flame base without first cutting HVAC ventilation, since entrained O2 intensifies the fire.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: SoFIE - Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction
entries.categoria: Solids / material flammability
entries.instalacion_hardware: CIR (insert) + flow duct in the MSG (ISS)
entries.investigador_responsable: NASA GRC SoFIE Project Team (P. Ferkul, S. Olson et al.)
entries.material_combustible: Plastics such as PMMA or Delrin
entries.condiciones: 10-40% O2; 0.2-1.5 atm; flow 0-30 cm/s (spacecraft ventilation range)
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Characterize ignition and flammability of spacecraft materials in exploration atmospheres (e.g. 10.2 psi, 32-34% O2)
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Umbrella program of five investigations to certify materials for the Artemis and Mars missions
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Certify all cabin polymers (PMMA, Delrin, fabrics) under low-pressure, high-O2 exploration atmospheres (up to 40% O2 and 0.2-1.5 atm) with real HVAC ventilation flows (0-30 cm/s).
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: SoFIE: Flammability correlation - Correlation of Flammability between Normal and Microgravity
entries.categoria: Solids / material flammability
entries.investigador_responsable: SoFIE Science Team
entries.material_combustible: Spacecraft engineering materials
entries.condiciones: Variable oxygen, pressure and flow
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Microgravity flammability map and comparison with NASA-STD-6001 Test 1
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Drop-tower data suggest NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Replace the single pass/fail criterion of NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 with multidimensional maps of the maximum oxygen concentration (MOC) as a function of forced-flow velocity and pressure.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: SoFIE: Growth and extinction - Fundamentals of Flame Growth and Extinction in Microgravity
entries.categoria: Solids / material flammability
entries.investigador_responsable: SoFIE Science Team
entries.material_combustible: Solid plastic spheres (PMMA)
entries.condiciones: Gravity, flow, O2, pressure, size, preheating
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Complete history of flame growth, spread and decay
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Links 1 g flammability to microgravity through a canonical spherical geometry
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Include the solid's internal preheating and surface curvature in predictive radiative-extinction models.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: SoFIE: Thermal and species fields - Thermal and Species Field Effects on Material Flammability
entries.categoria: Solids / material flammability
entries.investigador_responsable: SoFIE Science Team
entries.material_combustible: Thin solid fuels
entries.condiciones: Fuel thickness and ambient pressure
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Separate flame spread due to the thermal field from that due to the species field (radiative extinction)
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Can define the critical thickness, velocity or O2 for a material to be intrinsically safe
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Set minimum safe thicknesses for cabin coatings and plastic films below the thermal/species spread threshold.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: SoFIE: External heat flux - External Heat Flux Effects on Ignitability and Suppression of Materials in Microgravity
entries.categoria: Solids / material flammability
entries.investigador_responsable: SoFIE Science Team
entries.material_combustible: Materials in exploration atmospheres
entries.condiciones: Low forced flow with external radiant heat
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Ignition time and time to extinction after applying a suppressant
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: The critical heat flux for ignition in microgravity can be half that in normal gravity
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Cut the maximum allowed radiant heat flux near electronics and cables in spacecraft by 50% relative to the terrestrial standard; 2) Increase thermal insulation in power racks.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: SoFIE: Narrow Channel - Narrow Channel as a 1-g Flammability Test Method
entries.categoria: Solids / material flammability
entries.investigador_responsable: S. L. Olson / SoFIE Science Team
entries.material_combustible: Representative thick solid fuel
entries.condiciones: Opposed flow, O2 and pressure
entries.descripcion_objetivo: See whether a narrow channel in 1 g reproduces flammability in microgravity
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Possible ground test that mimics microgravity flames by suppressing buoyant plumes
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Adopt the Narrow Channel Apparatus in ground laboratories as a standard complementary method to, or replacement for, NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 to pre-certify space materials in 1 g.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: SAME - Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment
entries.categoria: Fire detection
entries.investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban (NASA GRC)
entries.material_combustible: Smoke from spacecraft materials (Teflon, Kapton, silicone, cellulose, overloaded lamp)
entries.condiciones: Particle size distribution and aerosol aging in microgravity
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Guide the design of space smoke detectors
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Smoke particles in microgravity differ from terrestrial ones (more agglomeration due to the lack of buoyancy)
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Redesign the laser-scattering optical chambers and threshold algorithms of space smoke detectors (Orion/Gateway/Lunar Lander) to detect the larger particle distributions produced by slow pyrolysis in 0 g.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: DAFT - Dust Aerosol measurement Feasibility Test
entries.categoria: Fire detection
entries.investigador_responsable: NASA GRC Aerosol Team
entries.fecha_periodo: Recent (year not stated in the guide)
entries.material_combustible: Background aerosols and dust on the ISS
entries.condiciones: Background particle levels in the cabin
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Measure background aerosol to reduce false alarms
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Fast detection with few false alarms by discriminating ambient dust from real smoke
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Add multi-wavelength discriminating filtering and lunar/ambient dust rejection to fire sensors to avoid false alarms from suspended dust after EVAs.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Mist - Water Mist Fire Suppression experiment
entries.categoria: Suppression
entries.investigador_responsable: T. McKinnon (Colorado School of Mines)
entries.material_combustible: Premixed flame in a tube, several fuel/oxygen mixtures
entries.condiciones: Water droplet diameter and concentration
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Effectiveness of water mist in suppressing fire (replacement for Halon and CO2)
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: The first two of nine water-mist Portable Fire Extinguishers (PFE) reached the ISS in Dec. 2015 to replace the CO2 units
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Replace CO2 and Halon 1301 extinguishers with fine water-mist extinguishers (Water Mist PFE, droplets < 50 microns), removing the CO2 toxicity risk in a closed cabin.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: SOFBALL - Structure of Flame Balls at Low Lewis-number
entries.categoria: Llamas premezcladas
entries.investigador_responsable: P. Ronney (USC)
entries.material_combustible: Mezclas premezcladas muy pobres (H2/O2/diluyente)
entries.condiciones: Low Lewis number
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Study stationary flame balls controlled by diffusion and radiation
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: The weakest flames ever burned (~1 W); some lasted more than 40 min without going out
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Lower the design lower flammability limit (LFL) for hydrogen and light-gas (low Lewis number) leaks in space habitats, since they can sustain stationary ~1 W flame balls below the terrestrial limit.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Candle Flames - Candle Flames in non-buoyant atmospheres
entries.categoria: Existencia y estabilidad de llama
entries.investigador_responsable: D. L. Dietrich et al. (NASA GRC)
entries.material_combustible: Paraffin candle
entries.condiciones: Long-duration microgravity, quiescent air
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Verify whether a flame can exist without natural convection
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Burned for more than 45 min as a faint blue hemisphere and at lower O2 than on Earth; oscillates as it nears extinction
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Drop the assumption that turning off ventilation immediately self-extinguishes a fire in quiescent air; 2) Keep thermal/UV monitoring for faint blue hemispherical flames that persist by pure diffusion.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: SCWM - Super-Critical Water Mixture
entries.categoria: Procesos supercríticos
entries.investigador_responsable: NASA-CNES Joint Team
entries.material_combustible: Mezcla agua-Na2SO4 (0.5% p/v)
entries.condiciones: Above the critical point (T > 374 °C, P > 22.1 MPa), with temperature gradients
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Formation and transport of salt precipitates in supercritical water
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Relevant to SCWO (supercritical water oxidation) reactors for life support and waste recycling
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Redesign walls and flow in life-support (ECLSS) SCWO reactors to avoid clogging and corrosion from inorganic salt (Na2SO4) precipitation without gravitational settling.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Cool Flames (initiative) - Cool Flames in the CIR
entries.categoria: Cool flames
entries.investigador_responsable: F. A. Williams / Nayagam / Dietrich
entries.material_combustible: Several fuel types (heavy alkanes, heptane, decane)
entries.condiciones: Variable pressure and diluent concentration
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Conditions before the hot/cool flame transition, stability and spontaneous reignition
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Very weak flames (500-800 K), invisible to the naked eye, can reignite long after the visible flame went out
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Update post-fire procedures on the ISS/Artemis to require full cooling and controlled venting of partially oxidized vapours (formaldehyde/CO) before reopening compartments where a flame seemed to go out.
entries.fuente: NASA Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Finding: Flammability limit (FLEX, BASS)
entries.categoria: Seguridad contra incendios
entries.investigador_responsable: FLEX and BASS hardware
entries.material_combustible: Heptane/methanol droplets and polymeric/cellulosic solids
entries.condiciones: Microgravity with low convective flow
entries.descripcion_objetivo: The flammability limit is lower in microgravity (heptane/methanol droplets and some solids)
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Terrestrial standards do not give the same safety margin
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: Lower the maximum allowed oxygen threshold (MOC) in space-material certification tables by an extra 2-4% O2 relative to 1 g ground tests.
entries.fuente: FLEX, BASS (NASA Guide 2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Finding: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 standard test (BASS)
entries.categoria: Seguridad contra incendios
entries.investigador_responsable: Equipo BASS / SoFIE
entries.material_combustible: Materiales certificados bajo NASA-STD-6001
entries.condiciones: Comparison of 1 g upward burning vs 0 g with slow forced flow
entries.descripcion_objetivo: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative: materials burn at lower oxygen in microgravity
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Ground tests can underestimate the fire risk in orbit
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: Replace or complement NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 with slow opposed-flow tests and a Narrow Channel apparatus calibrated with BASS and SoFIE data.
entries.fuente: BASS (NASA Guide 2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Finding: Spread against the flow (RITS / BASS)
entries.categoria: Seguridad contra incendios
entries.investigador_responsable: Radiative Ignition and Transition to Spread / BASS
entries.material_combustible: Thin and thick solids
entries.condiciones: Low forced flow (< 10 cm/s) in microgravity
entries.descripcion_objetivo: At low flow the flame spreads against the flow (upwind, toward fresh oxygen), the opposite of normal gravity
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Changes how fire spread is modelled and where to place sensors/firebreaks in spacecraft
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: Reverse the geometry of firebreak barriers and the placement of thermal sensors in ducts/racks so they also watch upstream (toward the ventilation air inlet).
entries.fuente: Radiative Ignition and Transition to Spread (NASA Guide 2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Finding: Spacecraft ventilation (~10 cm/s)
entries.categoria: Seguridad contra incendios
entries.investigador_responsable: Flame-spread studies over solids (BASS)
entries.material_combustible: Cabin polymers and fabrics
entries.condiciones: Typical cabin ventilation velocity (~10 cm/s)
entries.descripcion_objetivo: ~10 cm/s (typical ventilation velocity) coincides with the minimum of the flammability curve and the maximum spread
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Nominal spacecraft ventilation worsens a fire and maximizes the burning rate
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: Automate an immediate HVAC ventilation shutoff (flow to 0 cm/s) on detecting smoke or flame radiation, before discharging the extinguishing agent.
entries.fuente: Flame-spread studies over solids (NASA Guide 2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Finding: Localized nitrogen suppression (BASS)
entries.categoria: Seguridad contra incendios
entries.investigador_responsable: Equipo BASS
entries.material_combustible: PMMA spheres and plates
entries.condiciones: Local N2 jet applied to a burning sample
entries.descripcion_objetivo: A local nitrogen jet can strengthen the flame and keep it alive even after the main flow is turned off
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Where to apply the suppressant is not obvious in microgravity; a misdirected jet entrains oxygen toward the flame
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: Redesign extinguisher nozzles with total-flooding diffusers or enveloping mist instead of narrow inert-gas jets that induce O2 mixing.
entries.fuente: BASS (NASA Guide 2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Finding: Cool flames and spontaneous reignition (FLEX)
entries.categoria: Seguridad contra incendios
entries.investigador_responsable: Equipo FLEX
entries.material_combustible: Liquid hydrocarbon fuels
entries.condiciones: After the visible hot flame goes out
entries.descripcion_objetivo: After the visible flame goes out, a cool flame can keep burning and reignite spontaneously
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Fire invisible to the naked eye; high risk of late reignition
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: Add mid-wave IR cameras and CO/formaldehyde sensors to verify complete chemical (not just visual) extinction after a fire.
entries.fuente: FLEX (NASA Guide 2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Finding: Smoke detection in microgravity (SAME, DAFT)
entries.categoria: Seguridad contra incendios
entries.investigador_responsable: SAME and DAFT hardware
entries.material_combustible: Space cabin materials
entries.condiciones: No natural convection -> longer smoke residence time
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Smoke particle size in microgravity is very different from that on Earth
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Terrestrial detectors would look for the wrong signal
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: Recalibrate optical scattering angles and detection algorithms for the large agglomerated particles typical of microgravity.
entries.fuente: SAME, DAFT (NASA Guide 2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Finding: Ease of ignition in low gravity
entries.categoria: Seguridad contra incendios
entries.investigador_responsable: NASA GRC Flammability Team
entries.material_combustible: Cabin polymers and composites
entries.condiciones: Low gravity / microgravity with external radiation
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Materials ignite more easily in low gravity; the critical heat flux can be half
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Higher ignition risk from electrical overloads or radiant sources
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: Halve the maximum allowed temperature/heat flux on surfaces near cables and batteries; reinforce fast-acting circuit breakers.
entries.fuente: Models and parabolic flights (NASA Guide 2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Finding: Debunking 3 misconceptions about fire in space
entries.categoria: Seguridad contra incendios
entries.investigador_responsable: Summary of the NASA safety chapter
entries.material_combustible: Gases, liquids and solids in microgravity
entries.condiciones: Quiescent microgravity and slow flow
entries.descripcion_objetivo: It was believed that a steady fire cannot exist without convection, that it self-extinguishes without ventilation, and that terrestrial standards are conservative
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: All three assumptions proved false in real orbital tests
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: Update all crew training manuals and aerospace engineering standards to remove the 3 false assumptions.
entries.fuente: Safety chapter summary (NASA Guide 2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: Finding: Water-mist extinguishers on the ISS (Mist)
entries.categoria: Seguridad contra incendios
entries.investigador_responsable: Equipo Mist / ISS Program
entries.material_combustible: Class A/B/C cabin fires on the ISS
entries.condiciones: Fine water-mist discharge in microgravity
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Water-mist extinguishers were developed; the first two of nine reached the ISS in Dec. 2015
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Definitive replacement of CO2 units in the US segment of the ISS
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: Standardize water-mist extinguishers in orbital modules to avoid a lethal CO2 build-up after a discharge.
entries.fuente: Mist (NASA Guide 2015)

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: MHD flow and nucleation in Zr64Ni36 (Cycles 9, 19, 22, 23, 26, 29)
entries.categoria: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
entries.investigador_responsable: R. W. Hyers, G. P. Bracker (WPI / UMass), D. M. Matson, K. F. Kelton
entries.material_combustible: Molten metal alloy Zr64Ni36 (8.0 mm sphere, sigma = 7.271e5 S/m)
entries.condiciones: Electromagnetic levitation in microgravity; T = 1040-1760 K; heater current 17.5-55.7 A; positioner 140.8-191.7 A; 458 CFD files + 2 telemetry CSVs in part-01
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Characterize MHD flow velocity, Reynolds number and shear-strain rate during cooling to recalescence, to study cavitation/flow-induced dynamic nucleation
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: In Cycles 19, 22, 23 the flow is laminar (Re = 0.69-0.92, shear = 5.6-6.5 1/s); in Cycles 26 and 29, with the heater on, the flow is initially turbulent (Re > 600 above 1720 K and 1460 K) and crosses the laminar-turbulent transition; the cooling rate (0.02-1.33 °C/s) was an order of magnitude lower than in the SRD (10 °C/s)
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Switch from the laminar model to the RNG k-epsilon turbulent model above 1460 K (Cycle 29) and 1720 K (Cycle 26); 2) Recalculate the target shear-strain rate for the real slow cooling rates (0.02-1.33 °C/s) so that concentration profiles around subcritical nuclei do not interact; 3) Turn off the heater control voltage (0.000 V) during the free-cooling phase.
entries.fuente: Carpeta part-01: PSI-166_Reports_Updated ZrNi Report.pdf & 458 archivos Raw Data ZrNi

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: Flow characterization in Cu50Zr50 (Cycles 3, 4, 9, 10, 16, 18)
entries.categoria: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
entries.investigador_responsable: R. W. Hyers, G. P. Bracker (WPI / UMass)
entries.material_combustible: Metallic-glass-forming alloy Cu50Zr50 (6.5 mm sphere, sigma = 7.05e5 S/m)
entries.condiciones: T = 950-1455 K; heater 0.000 V (17.5 A); positioner 1.498-6.659 V (70.3-215.6 A); 256 CFD files in part-01
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Correlate EML coil voltage with maximum velocity and shear rate near the liquidus temperature and recalescence (950-1075 K)
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Fully laminar flow throughout cooling (Re = 0.007 to 1.44 << 600; shear-strain = 0.519 to 5.41 1/s), but the real cooling rate (0.31 to 2.01 K/s) was much slower than the 10 K/s specified in the SRD
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Review and recalculate the shear-strain-rate target specific to Cu50Zr50 at low cooling rates (0.31-2.01 K/s), considering its own chemical and thermodynamic driving forces; 2) Prefer the low positioner-voltage setup (1.498 V, Cycles 9-10) to minimize pole-equator asymmetry (2.7x vs 24x in Cycles 3-4).

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: Quasicrystal nucleation in Ti39.5Zr39.5Ni21 (Cycles 11, 49, 50, 53, 55, 62, 64, 65, 66)
entries.categoria: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
entries.investigador_responsable: R. W. Hyers, G. P. Bracker, K. F. Kelton (Washington U.)
entries.material_combustible: Quasicrystal-forming alloy Ti39.5Zr39.5Ni21 (6.0 mm sphere, liquidus 1093 K)
entries.condiciones: Undercooling of ~150 K (recalescence at 980-1032 K); positioner 3.87-9.39 V; 12 FluentMagData zip files and 3 reports in part-01
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Check whether the shear-strain rate meets the SRD requirement to avoid collisions between the diffusion fields of critical and subcritical nuclei
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Laminar flow (Re = 0.30-1.33), but the shear-strain rate (3.10-9.45 1/s) exceeds the strict subcritical-cluster limit (0.05-0.5 1/s); also, Cycles 64-66 cooled 2.5-3x faster (-25.5 to -30.9 K/s) and the other 6 cycles much slower (-2.18 to -7.95 K/s) than the SRD's 10 K/s
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Recalculate the SRD shear-strain-rate targets separately for the fast-cooling (Cycles 64-66, ~28 K/s) and slow-cooling cycles (Cycles 11, 49, 50, 53, 55, 62, ~2-8 K/s); 2) Lower the positioner voltage in Cycles 65-66 (from 9.39 V to <= 3.87 V) to bring the shear rate down toward the diffusion-controlled regime (0.05-0.5 1/s).
entries.fuente: Carpeta part-01: PSI-166_Analyzed Data_Updated Fluid Flow Results Modeling TiZrNi.pdf

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: Turbulence and viscosity in Sb-doped molten germanium (Ge Batch 2.1)
entries.categoria: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
entries.investigador_responsable: G. P. Bracker, R. W. Hyers (for the SEMITHERM group / Samwer & Luo)
entries.material_combustible: Antimony (Sb)-doped germanium (10^19 /cm3, 8.0 mm sphere, sigma = 1.52e6 S/m)
entries.condiciones: T = 1158-1310 K; oscillating-drop method; 33 Raw Data Ge files and Final Ge Report.pdf in part-01
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Explain the 1 to 2 orders-of-magnitude discrepancy between the viscosity measured in ISS-EML (0.0029 Pa·s), parabolic flights (0.0124-0.0136 Pa·s) and a rotating cup on Earth (4.55e-4 Pa·s)
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Both the video of chaotic oxide rafts and the CFD model show the flow is highly turbulent throughout the cycle (Re = 69,400-72,700 at maximum T and Re = 6,450-6,600 just before recalescence), damping the oscillations and artificially inflating the apparent viscosity
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Modify the oscillating-drop damping equation to include turbulent eddy viscosity (from the RNG k-epsilon model) so turbulent damping is discounted; 2) Drastically reduce positioning and heating currents for highly conductive semiconductor samples (1.52e6 S/m).
entries.fuente: Carpeta part-01: PSI-166_Reports_Final Ge Report.pdf & npj Microgravity (2022) 10.1038/s41526-022-00238-z

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: Simulation stability and flow in Vit106 metallic glass (Cycles 1, 8, 60, 68)
entries.categoria: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
entries.investigador_responsable: G. P. Bracker, R. W. Hyers
entries.material_combustible: Bulk-metallic-glass-forming alloy Vit106 (sigma = 6.00e5 S/m)
entries.condiciones: Recalescence at 850-875 K; high viscosity (8.37-15.1 Pa·s); cooling rates of 0.85 to 19.63 °C/s
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Characterize extremely slow flow in a very viscous undercooled liquid down to recalescence
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: At low temperatures the VFT viscosity fit grows excessively and makes the CFD simulations numerically unstable; with the KKZNT fit the flow is stable and ultra-laminar (Re = 4.49e-5 to 7.23e-4; shear-strain = 0.031 to 0.274 1/s)
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Replace the VFT viscosity law with the KKZNT formulation using a Heaviside step function at low temperatures (T < T* = 1471.7 K) to ensure numerical stability in ANSYS Fluent; 2) Recalculate the shear-strain-rate target for each cycle's cooling rate (0.85 to 19.63 °C/s).
entries.fuente: Carpeta part-01: PSI-166_Analyzed Data_Updated Vit106 Simulation Results.pdf

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-25: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids - II)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-25: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II) in the ISS MSG
entries.categoria: Sólidos / inflamabilidad y supresión en microgravedad (Repositorio NASA PSI-25)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / modified SPICE flow duct (7.6 x 7.6 cm section)
entries.investigador_responsable: S. L. Olson, P. V. Ferkul (NASA GRC), J. S. T'ien (CWRU), C. Fernandez-Pello (UC Berkeley), I. S. Wichman (MSU), F. J. Miller (SDSU)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS Expeditions 38-40 (2014) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-25
entries.material_combustible: Flat black and clear PMMA plates (1.2-6.35 mm), PMMA cylinders (6.35-12.7 mm), PMMA spheres (19 mm), SIBAL fabric (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass), thin cotton, Nomex and Ultem film
entries.condiciones: Opposed and concurrent forced flow from 0 to 53 cm/s (high sensitivity at 0.4-10 cm/s); N2 vitiation from 21.8% down to 13.5% O2 (MOC/LOI determination); cabin pressure ~100.5-101.5 kPa; radiometer, thermocouples and HD video
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Determine flame spread rates (Vf), radiative extinction limits (low flow) and convective blowoff limits (high flow), and compare the limiting oxygen index (MOC) in 0 g with NASA-STD-6001 Test 1
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: PMMA and SIBAL fabric samples sustain stable faint blue flames at ultra-low flows (0.5-2 cm/s) with O2 concentrations up to 2.5-3.5% below the 1 g terrestrial limit; stepping the fan down (step-down flow) reveals thermal hysteresis before radiative extinction
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Lower the MOC certification threshold for cabin polymers and textiles to <= 15.0% O2 for slow-ventilation regimes (0.5-8 cm/s); 2) Add two-branch extinction curves (radiative quenching < 1 cm/s and convective blowoff > 30 cm/s) to the Orion/Gateway fire code; 3) Require a waiting time after ventilation shutoff (> 60 s) because of the thermal inertia of thick solids (PMMA >= 3.2 mm).
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-25

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-68: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2 (FLEX-2) in the ISS CIR / MDCA
entries.categoria: Combustión de gotas aisladas, mezclas bicomponente y llamas frías (Repositorio NASA PSI-68)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
entries.investigador_responsable: F. A. Williams (UCSD), F. L. Dryer (Princeton), V. Nayagam (CWRU), D. L. Dietrich & M. C. Hicks (NASA GRC), T. I. Farouk (USC)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS Expeditions 29-45 (2012-2015) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-68
entries.material_combustible: Free or SiC-fiber-supported liquid droplets (D0 = 1.8 to 5.0 mm): n-heptane, n-decane, n-octane, n-dodecane, methanol, ethanol, PRF blends (n-heptane/iso-octane), jet-fuel surrogates (decane/propylbenzene) and binary droplet arrays
entries.condiciones: Ambient pressure 0.5 to 3.0 atm (50.6 to 304.0 kPa); O2 concentration 12% to 40%; N2, CO2, He and Xe diluents; quiescent environment (0 cm/s) and slow convective flow by translation (0.5 to 22 cm/s); droplet spacing L/D0 = 2 to 12
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Quantify the burning-rate constant K (d^2 law: D^2 = D0^2 - K*t), soot-shell formation, radiative extinction of the hot flame, transition to two-stage combustion (cool flames at 550-750 K) and droplet-droplet interaction
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Large linear alkanes (n-heptane, n-decane, n-dodecane) undergo radiative extinction of the visible hot flame but keep vaporizing through invisible cool flames governed by NTC (negative temperature coefficient) chemistry, which can produce an explosive vapour-cloud reignition; in alcohols (methanol/ethanol), absorption of the water produced in the flame causes abrupt extinction
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Integrate low-temperature kinetic sub-mechanisms (NTC / RO2 alkyl peroxides) into space propulsion and safety CFD models to predict cool flames (550-750 K); 2) Install UV (OH* at 310 nm) + UV/visible (HCHO* at 395 nm) and IR optical diagnostics in combustion chambers and habitats; 3) Raise the CO2/N2 dilution margin by at least +4% to suppress both the hot-flame and cool-flame branches in heavy hydrocarbons.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-68

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-26: BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-26: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS) in the ISS MSG
entries.categoria: Sólidos / inflamabilidad, propagación upwind y supresión con N2 (Repositorio NASA PSI-26)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / SPICE duct with N2 suppressant nozzle
entries.investigador_responsable: S. L. Olson, P. V. Ferkul (NASA GRC), J. S. T'ien (CWRU), C. Fernandez-Pello, I. S. Wichman, F. J. Miller
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS Expeditions 30-31 (2012) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-26
entries.material_combustible: PMMA spheres (20 mm), flat PMMA plates (1.5 mm), paraffin and porous wax candles, SIBAL fabric (cotton/fiberglass)
entries.condiciones: Cabin air (21% O2 down to 15.8% O2), 1 atm (100.4-101.3 kPa), forced flow from 0 to 35 cm/s and application of a localized N2 jet
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Investigate burning and extinction of solid fuels in microgravity, upwind spread geometry and the effectiveness of nitrogen jets
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Showed for the first time on the ISS that spread at low flows (<10 cm/s) happens only against the wind (upwind), that materials burn at lower O2 than in NASA-STD-6001 Test 1, and that a slow local N2 jet intensifies the flame by entraining surrounding O2
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Prohibit narrow N2-jet extinguisher nozzles without first cutting ventilation; 2) Reorient thermal sensors upstream of electronic components; 3) Replace the one-dimensional criterion of NASA-STD-6001 Test 1.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-26

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-62: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling (FGM & Two-Color Tomography)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-62: Concurrent flame-spread modelling with Flamelet Generated Manifolds (FGM) and two-color tomography (BASS/BASS-II)
entries.categoria: Modelado CFD / FGM y Diagnóstico Óptico Tomográfico de Sólidos (Repositorio NASA PSI-62)
entries.instalacion_hardware: High-fidelity CFD simulation (UFGM / OpenFOAM / ANSYS) validated against ISS MSG video (BASS PSI-26 & BASS-II PSI-25)
entries.investigador_responsable: PSI-62 modelling team / BASS and BASS-II associate investigators (NASA GRC / CWRU)
entries.material_combustible: Flat PMMA plates and SIBAL fabric (optical data from BASS PSI-26 and BASS-II PSI-25)
entries.condiciones: Concurrent flow of 0.5 to 35 cm/s, 16.0-21.0% O2, reconstruction of the flame temperature field and soot volume fraction by two-color pyrometry/tomography
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Develop Unsteady Flamelet Generated Manifold (UFGM) models coupled with soot radiation and solid pyrolysis to predict concurrent spread and extinction in microgravity
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: The UFGM model reproduces the flame structure, base liftoff and radiative-extinction hysteresis at >10x lower computational cost than direct detailed chemistry, validated against the BASS two-color tomography temperature maps
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Adopt pre-integrated Unsteady Flamelet Generated Manifold (UFGM) tables with non-adiabatic radiative losses in cabin-certification CFD codes; 2) Calibrate soot-emission models with volume-fraction profiles measured by two-color optical tomography.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-62

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-69: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) in the ISS CIR / MDCA
entries.categoria: Combustión de gotas líquidas, supresores gaseosos y descubrimiento de Cool Flames (Repositorio NASA PSI-69)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
entries.investigador_responsable: F. A. Williams (UCSD), D. L. Dietrich (NASA GRC), V. Nayagam (CWRU), F. L. Dryer (Princeton), B. D. Shaw (UC Davis)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS Expeditions 19-30 (2009-2012) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-69
entries.material_combustible: Isolated n-heptane and methanol droplets (D0 = 1.8 to 5.0 mm), free or on SiC fiber
entries.condiciones: Pressure 0.5 to 3.0 atm (50.6 to 304.0 kPa); 14% to 40% O2; inert suppressant gases N2, CO2, He, Xe and SF6; convective flow 0 to 10 cm/s
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Map the flammability and extinction limits of liquid fuel droplets under different gaseous suppressant agents in microgravity
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Landmark ISS discovery of self-sustaining cool flames on n-heptane droplets after radiative extinction of the visible hot flame; showed that CO2 suppresses through radiative reabsorption, He acts through high thermal diffusivity, and SF6 increases radiative losses
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Raise the design concentration of inert agents (N2, CO2) by +3 to +5% relative to terrestrial NFPA standards; 2) Add spectral monitoring of excited formaldehyde (HCHO*) and mid-infrared after any apparent extinction of liquid hydrocarbons.
