entries.codigo_corto: PSI-98: SAFFIRE-I (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - I)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-98: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - I (SAFFIRE-I) on the Cygnus OA-6 vehicle
entries.categoria: Incendio a gran escala en nave espacial real (Repositorio NASA PSI-98)
entries.instalacion_hardware: Autonomous SAFFIRE module on the Northrop Grumman Cygnus OA-6 cargo vehicle (after undocking from the ISS)
entries.investigador_responsable: G. A. Ruff, D. L. Urban (NASA GRC), C. Fernandez-Pello, J. S. T'ien, S. L. Olson, P. V. Ferkul
entries.fecha_periodo: June 2016 (Cygnus OA-6 mission) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-98
entries.material_combustible: Large continuous panel of SIBAL fabric (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass), 0.40 m wide x 0.94 m long
entries.condiciones: Concurrent forced flow of 20 cm/s in a large-section flow tunnel; nominal air ~21% O2 and 101.3 kPa (1 atm); hot-wire ignition at the upstream and downstream edges
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Characterize for the first time the growth of a large (~1 m) fire in real microgravity, checking whether the flame grows indefinitely or reaches a steady limiting size
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Unlike terrestrial fires, which accelerate exponentially, in microgravity at 20 cm/s the flame quickly reached a steady limiting length (~20-25 cm) and a constant spread rate (~1.6 mm/s), owing to the radiative balance and O2 consumption in the boundary layer
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Update cabin emergency-response models with the large-scale steady spread rate and the fast pressure/temperature rise in a closed volume; 2) Validate that cutting ventilation immediately stops a 0.4 m-wide flame front.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-98

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-99: SAFFIRE-II (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - II)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-99: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - II (SAFFIRE-II, 9 samples) on the Cygnus OA-5 vehicle
entries.categoria: Límites MOC de materiales estructurales y textiles a escala real (Repositorio NASA PSI-99)
entries.instalacion_hardware: Autonomous SAFFIRE module on the Cygnus OA-5 cargo vehicle (sample holder with 9 panels of 5 cm x 29 cm)
entries.investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban, G. A. Ruff, P. V. Ferkul (NASA GRC), Equipo Internacional SAFFIRE
entries.fecha_periodo: November 2016 (Cygnus OA-5 mission) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-99
entries.material_combustible: 9 samples (5 x 29 cm): SIBAL fabric, Nomex HT90-40, silicone sheets of 3 thicknesses (0.25, 0.60 and 1.57 mm), 10 mm PMMA plates, flat and with longitudinal grooved ribs, and cotton fabric
entries.condiciones: Forced flows of 20 cm/s and 30 cm/s; cabin atmosphere (~20.8-21.0% O2 initially, falling progressively to ~17.2% O2 through consumption in the Cygnus module); ~101.0 kPa
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Evaluate the effect of material thickness, surface geometry (grooves/edges) and O2 decline on flammability in microgravity versus NASA-STD-6001 Test 1
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: The thin silicone sheets (0.25 and 0.60 mm) burned vigorously while the thick one (1.57 mm) went out; the machined grooves in the thick PMMA (10 mm) acted as thermal fins that sustained spread where an identical flat plate self-extinguished
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Penalize in certification protocols geometries with exposed edges, grooves or ribs in thick polymers (PMMA/polycarbonate), since they sustain the flame when the flat surface does not burn; 2) Restrict silicone membranes thinner than 1.5 mm in ducts with flow >= 20 cm/s.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-99

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-100: SAFFIRE-III (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - III)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-100: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - III (SAFFIRE-III) on the Cygnus OA-7 vehicle
entries.categoria: Efecto de alta velocidad de ventilación en incendio a gran escala (Repositorio NASA PSI-100)
entries.instalacion_hardware: Autonomous SAFFIRE module on the Cygnus OA-7 cargo vehicle (continuous 0.40 m x 0.94 m panel)
entries.investigador_responsable: G. A. Ruff, D. L. Urban, P. V. Ferkul (NASA GRC), C. Fernandez-Pello, J. S. T'ien
entries.fecha_periodo: June 2017 (Cygnus OA-7 mission) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-100
entries.material_combustible: Large continuous panel of SIBAL fabric (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass, 0.40 m x 0.94 m)
entries.condiciones: Concurrent forced flow raised to 30 cm/s (50% higher than in SAFFIRE-I); ~20.9% O2, 101.3 kPa; CO2, O2, pressure and radiometry measurements
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Determine how raising the ventilation velocity from 20 cm/s (SAFFIRE-I) to 30 cm/s (SAFFIRE-III) affects flame spread rate, heat release rate (HRR) and O2 consumption
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Raising the flow from 20 to 30 cm/s increased the concurrent spread rate by ~40% (from ~1.6 to ~2.25 mm/s) and the thermal power proportionally, confirming that convective O2 supply directly controls the pyrolysis rate in large fires in 0 g
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Limit the maximum air velocity in space-habitat corridors and plenums to < 15 cm/s; 2) Size post-fire pressure relief and CO/CO2 scrubbing systems for heat release rates that scale linearly with ventilation velocity.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-100

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-101: SAME-R (Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-101: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight (SAME-R) in the ISS MSG
entries.categoria: Distribución de tamaño y envejecimiento de aerosoles de humo espacial (Repositorio NASA PSI-101)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with PAMS (particle counter), aerosol moment meter, ionization (ISS smoke detector) and laser scattering (Orion smoke detector)
entries.investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban, G. A. Ruff (NASA GRC), G. W. Mulholland (NIST / U. Maryland), T. Cleary (NIST)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS Expedition 23-24 (2010) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-101
entries.material_combustible: Samples pyrolyzed by thermal overload: Kapton and Teflon (PTFE) wire insulation, silicone rubber, cellulose paper, PMMA and lamp-oil wick
entries.condiciones: Duct flow velocities of 1.5 to 6.0 cm/s; controlled aerosol aging (aging chamber, 0 to 600 s); ~20.9% O2, 101.3 kPa
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Quantify the count median diameter (CMD), Sauter mean diameter (SMD) and aging coagulation of smoke from spacecraft materials to calibrate the ISS and Orion smoke detectors
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: In microgravity the lack of a buoyant plume keeps pyrolyzed vapour near the hot source longer, producing primary particles and agglomerates significantly larger (CMD 0.3 to 1.2 microns) than in 1 g, which lowers the sensitivity of conventional ionization detectors and favours laser-scattering optical ones
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Replace ionization smoke detectors (designed for ultrafine particles < 0.1 microns in 1 g) with laser-scattering photoelectric detectors calibrated for the 0.3-1.5 micron range measured in SAME-R; 2) Include coagulation-compensation algorithms for slow transport through the cabin.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-101

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-102: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME) in the ISS MSG
entries.categoria: Generación y detección temprana de humo por pirólisis en microgravedad (Repositorio NASA PSI-102)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / ISS smoke detector (ionization) and Space Shuttle detector (photoelectric) + TEM thermal precipitator
entries.investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban, G. A. Ruff (NASA GRC), G. W. Mulholland, Z. G. Yuan, T. Cleary
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS Expedition 15 (July 2007) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-102
entries.material_combustible: Teflon (PTFE), Kapton, silicone rubber, cellulose (paper) and lamp oil (lamp oil wick)
entries.condiciones: Flameless pyrolysis (non-flaming overheat) at different heating powers and ventilation flows of 1.0 to 7.0 cm/s; direct sampling onto transmission electron microscopy (TEM) grids
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Establish the baseline fractal morphology and size-distribution moments of smoke from aerospace materials to compare the response of the Shuttle and ISS detectors
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Overheated Teflon produces ultrafine particles (~0.06-0.12 microns) invisible to the standard optical detector without coagulation, while silicone and cellulose produce large fractal chains (>0.5 microns) that saturate the photoelectric sensor before the ionization one
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Deploy dual-wavelength (blue + near-infrared) smoke sensors that measure the size-moment ratio (mean diameter) at the same time, to tell Teflon/wire pyrolysis (small particles) from silicone/cellulose smoke or ambient dust.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-102

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-10: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Flame Design (ACME) in the ISS CIR
entries.categoria: Llamas de difusión esféricas normales e inversas y control estequiométrico de hollín (Repositorio NASA PSI-10)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / ACME insert with a porous spherical burner
entries.investigador_responsable: R. L. Axelbaum (Washington U. in St. Louis), P. B. Sunderland (U. Maryland), D. L. Urban (NASA GRC)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2019-2020 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-10
entries.material_combustible: Ethylene (C2H4) and methane (CH4) with N2 dilution in normal (fuel inside) and inverse (oxidizer inside) diffusion-flame configurations
entries.condiciones: Stoichiometric mixture fraction Z_st varied between 0.06 and 0.65 (O2 from 15.6% to 40%); pressure 1 atm (101.3 kPa); quiescent 6.4 mm porous spherical burner
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Show how designing the flame structure (controlling Z_st by moving N2 from the oxidizer to the fuel) allows operating in O2-enriched atmospheres with vigorous yet permanently soot-free flames
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Raising Z_st above the critical threshold (~0.35 for ethylene) carries soot precursors into the oxidizing zone before they nucleate; it also revealed quasi-steady extinction by radiative loss as the spherical flame radius grows
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Reconfigure space burners and incinerators by moving the diluent (N2/CO2) into the fuel stream to raise Z_st > 0.35, eliminating soot and excess thermal radiation even in O2-enriched exploration atmospheres.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-10

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-20: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator (ACME BRE) in the ISS CIR
entries.categoria: Emulación de inflamabilidad de polímeros y materiales sólidos mediante quemador gaseoso (Repositorio NASA PSI-20)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / flat 25 and 50 mm porous bronze burner with a thermal feedback loop
entries.investigador_responsable: J. G. Quintiere, P. B. Sunderland (U. Maryland), J. L. de Ris (FM Global), D. L. Urban (NASA GRC)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2019-2021 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-20
entries.material_combustible: Ethylene, methane and N2/CO2 blends programmed to match the heat of combustion, smoke point and heat of gasification (L_g) of PMMA, polyoxymethylene (Delrin), paper and ethanol
entries.condiciones: Fuel mass flow regulated in real time from the heat flux measured at the burner surface; O2 from 15.8% to 28%; pressure 70 to 101.3 kPa
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Validate the hypothesis that flammability and extinction of condensed solid materials in microgravity depend only on their mass-transfer B-number, heat of gasification, heat of combustion and smoke point
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: The BRE burner reproduced with high accuracy the extinction limits of hemispherical blue flames over real solids for long times (several minutes), without sample deformation or geometric consumption
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Use the BRE parameter matrix (heat of gasification L_g and B-number) to pre-screen candidate cabin polymers without burning hundreds of solid samples in orbit.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-20

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-21: ACME / CLD Flame (Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-21: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (ACME CLD) in the ISS CIR
entries.categoria: Llamas laminares de difusión en coflujo bajo dilución extrema y formación de hollín (Repositorio NASA PSI-21)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / ACME coaxial burner with multispectral optical diagnostics and a plenoptic camera
entries.investigador_responsable: M. B. Long, M. D. Smooke (Yale University), F. Takahashi (NASA GRC)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2017-2020 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-21
entries.material_combustible: Methane and ethylene highly diluted with N2 in air coflow in the CIR
entries.condiciones: Coflow velocity 2 to 30 cm/s; N2 dilution of the fuel up to the liftoff and blowoff limits; pressure 101.3 kPa
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Study the coupled chemical-fluid structure of lifted and sooting flames in microgravity to validate C1-C2 hydrocarbon kinetic mechanisms at dilution extremes
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Without buoyant acceleration, the base of the lifted flame (triple flame) stabilizes at much lower velocities and depends purely on the stoichiometric laminar flame speed and radiative losses
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Recalibrate the edge/triple-flame stabilization and soot-radiation sub-models in CFD codes for low-emission combustors and space burners.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-21

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-22: ACME / E-FIELD Flames (Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-22: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (ACME E-FIELD) in the ISS CIR
entries.categoria: Control electrohidrodinámico (EHD) de llamas y viento iónico en microgravedad (Repositorio NASA PSI-22)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / coaxial burner with a high-voltage electrode mesh (up to +/- 10 kV) and an ion-current ammeter
entries.investigador_responsable: D. Dunn-Rankin (UC Irvine), F. J. Weinberg (Imperial College), Z. G. Yuan (NASA GRC)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2018-2019 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-22
entries.material_combustible: Methane and ethylene (pure and N2-diluted) in a free jet or laminar coflow
entries.condiciones: Applied voltage 0 to +/- 10 kV between burner and collector mesh; measurement of chemi-ionization saturation current (H3O+, CHO+, charged soot particles); 1 atm
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Understand the relationship between electric-field voltage, chemical ion current and the induced ionic wind to control flame stability, length and soot emission in microgravity
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Without terrestrial buoyancy interfering, the electric field accelerates the ions formed in the reaction zone, dragging neutral molecules (ionic wind); this shortens the flame, suppresses soot completely and allows variable artificial gravity to be emulated
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Add high-voltage electrode rings/meshes (6-9 kV, < 1 W) to orbital burners and incinerators to replace mechanical fans with ionic-wind convection and eliminate soot emission.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-22

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-23: ACME / s-Flame (Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-23: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (ACME s-Flame) in the ISS CIR
entries.categoria: Dinámica unidimensional, inestabilidad pulsante y extinción radiativa en llamas esféricas (Repositorio NASA PSI-23)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / 6.4 mm porous spherical burner fed with H2, CH4 and C2H4
entries.investigador_responsable: C. K. Law (Princeton University), S. H. Tse (Rutgers), R. L. Axelbaum (WUSTL)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2017-2018 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-23
entries.material_combustible: Soot-free (hydrogen H2 and methane CH4) and sooting (ethylene C2H4) mixtures diluted with He, N2, Ar or CO2
entries.condiciones: Pure 1D spherical geometry in microgravity; effective Lewis number (Le) varied with helium/argon/CO2; mass flows of 0.3 to 5.0 mg/s
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Isolate the coupling between preferential diffusion (Lewis number), gas/soot radiative losses and pulsating instabilities before radiative or diffusive extinction
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Large-amplitude pulsating oscillations were observed near the radiative extinction limit when the Lewis number exceeds the critical threshold (Le > 1), confirming theoretical predictions impossible to observe in 1 g
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Include pulsating diffusive-thermal instability criteria (Le > 1) and CO2/H2O radiative reabsorption in spherical fire spread and extinction models for space cabins.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-23

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-39: Cool Flames Investigation (CFI) in the ISS CIR / MDCA
entries.categoria: Química de baja temperatura y combustión en dos etapas de hidrocarburos pesados y ésteres (Repositorio NASA PSI-39)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
entries.investigador_responsable: F. A. Williams (UCSD), V. Nayagam (CWRU), D. L. Dietrich & M. C. Hicks (NASA GRC), F. L. Dryer (Princeton)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2013-2017 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-39
entries.material_combustible: Droplets of n-decane, n-dodecane, heptane/iso-octane blends and methyl butanoate (biodiesel surrogate)
entries.condiciones: Droplets of 0.8 to 4.5 mm; pressures of 1.0 to 3.0 atm (101.3 to 304.0 kPa); O2 from 14% to 30% in N2/CO2; intensified UV (OH*) and visible/blue (HCHO*) cameras
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Systematically investigate the hot-to-cool flame transition regime (NTC, 550-800 K), second-stage induction times and diffusive extinction of cool flames
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Showed that while C7-C12 linear alkanes sustain long cool flames after radiative extinction of the hot flame, submillimetre oxygenated esters such as methyl butanoate show suppression of the NTC branch
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Differentiate in-orbit safety and suppression protocols by the liquid's molecular structure (linear alkanes with a high risk of invisible cool flames vs esters/alcohols without an NTC branch).
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-39

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-47: DAFT / DAFT-2 (Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-47: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test 1 & 2 (DAFT / DAFT-2) in the ISS cabin
entries.categoria: Conteo de partículas ultrafinas en cabina y viabilidad de fluidos capilares para P-Trak (Repositorio NASA PSI-47)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS cabin (USOS and Russian segments) / commercial TSI P-Trak condensation particle counter (CPC) modified for microgravity
entries.investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban, G. A. Ruff (NASA GRC), Risk Mitigation Team for SAME (PSI-102)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS Expeditions 12-16 (2006-2007) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-47
entries.material_combustible: ISS cabin background aerosol and ultrafine particles (< 0.1 microns) from crew activities and incipient combustion; isopropyl alcohol working fluid in a capillary wick
entries.condiciones: Ambient sampling in several ISS modules; cabin airflow 5 to 12 cm/s; capillary saturation test of the P-Trak wick in 0 g
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Verify that the TSI P-Trak condensation particle counter works correctly with capillary transport in microgravity (mitigating the risk for SAME PSI-102) and measure the background ultrafine-particle level on the ISS
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Capillary alcohol transport worked in 0 g; it was also found that the background ultrafine-particle concentration on the ISS is extremely low (< 100-500 particles/cm3 thanks to HEPA filters) except for sharp peaks during food cooking/heating, which gives an excellent signal-to-noise ratio for detecting early fires
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Exploit the low cabin background of ultrafine particles (thanks to HEPA filtering) by setting early pre-alarm thresholds on condensation-nucleus counts (CPC) for incipient electrical overloads; 2) Temporarily mask the pre-alarm in the food-warmer (galley) area.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-47

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-60: Computational and experimental analysis of SPICE data
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-60: Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Datasets (derived from PSI-107)
entries.categoria: Modelado CFD de punto de humo, oxidación de hollín y apertura de punta radiativa (Repositorio NASA PSI-60)
entries.instalacion_hardware: 2D/axisymmetric CFD simulation + SPICE experimental database from the ISS MSG (PSI-107)
entries.investigador_responsable: P. B. Sunderland (U. Maryland), D. L. Urban (NASA GRC), NASA PSI-60 grant investigators
entries.material_combustible: Ethylene, propylene, propane and n-butane in laminar air coflow
entries.condiciones: Nozzles of 1.1 to 4.1 mm; coflow velocities of 1 to 32 cm/s; transition from a closed soot-free flame to an open flame releasing soot at the tip (tip opening)
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Numerically model soot nucleation, surface growth and O2/OH oxidation in microgravity coflow flames to explain why the smoke point in 0 g is much lower than in 1 g
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: In microgravity the residence time in the high-temperature annular region is much longer, and radiative cooling of the tip quenches the soot oxidation zone (radiative tip quenching), releasing wings of unburned soot
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Couple optically thin/thick radiation models with OH- and O2-radical soot oxidation kinetics to predict sudden soot release (wing/tip opening) in space fires.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-60

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-106: SLICE (Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-106: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment (SLICE) in the ISS MSG
entries.categoria: Estabilización, estructura de borde y desprendimiento (liftoff) de llamas en coflujo (Repositorio NASA PSI-106)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / reconfigured SPICE hardware with color digital cameras and CH*/OH*/C2* filters
entries.investigador_responsable: M. B. Long, M. D. Smooke (Yale University), D. L. Urban (NASA GRC)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS Expedition 30-31 (2012) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-106
entries.material_combustible: Methane, ethylene and propane diluted with N2 in circular nozzles inside a coflow duct
entries.condiciones: Attached and lifted flames at coflow velocities of 1.5 to 30 cm/s; acoustic/pulsed disturbances
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Investigate the structure of partially premixed flames at the liftoff base (liftoff height) and the blowout limit without buoyancy
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Provided the first quantitative maps of CH* and C2* radical luminescence together with soot pyrometry in lifted flames on the ISS, a direct bridge to the design of ACME CLD Flame (PSI-21)
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Design flame holders in space combustion systems taking into account that liftoff height in 0 g is more sensitive to the coflow momentum deficit.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-106

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-107: SPICE (Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-107: Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment (SPICE) in the ISS MSG
entries.categoria: Determinación experimental del punto de humeo (smoke point) en microgravedad (Repositorio NASA PSI-107)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / miniature wind tunnel with hot-wire anemometry and a retractable igniter
entries.investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban (NASA GRC), P. B. Sunderland (U. Maryland), G. M. Faeth (U. Michigan), Z. G. Yuan
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS Expedition 18-19 (2009) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-107
entries.material_combustible: Six gaseous hydrocarbons: methane, propane, n-butane, ethylene, propylene and blends in air coflow
entries.condiciones: Nozzle diameters of 1.1, 2.0 and 4.1 mm; air coflow velocity 0.8 to 35 cm/s; cabin pressure 101.3 kPa, ~21% O2
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Determine the luminous flame length and the critical fuel flow at the transition from a soot-free to a soot-emitting flame (smoke point) in microgravity
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Smoke points in microgravity are 2 to 5 times lower than in terrestrial gravity, owing to the lack of buoyant acceleration and radiative quenching of the flame tip; raising the coflow velocity restores tip oxidation and raises the smoke-point threshold
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Apply a 3x safety reduction factor to terrestrial smoke-point tables (ASTM D1322) when assessing soot propensity and HEPA filter loading in space fires.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-107

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-108: STDCE-1 (Surface Tension Driven Convection Experiment - 1)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-108: Surface Tension Driven Convection Experiment - 1 (STDCE-1) on USML-1 STS-50
entries.categoria: Convección termocapilar de Marangoni e hidrodinámica de superficies libres calientes (Repositorio NASA PSI-108)
entries.instalacion_hardware: Spacelab USML-1 (Space Shuttle Columbia STS-50) / 10 cm cylindrical chamber with CO2 laser heating (CT) and an immersed heater (CF) + IR thermography and PIV
entries.investigador_responsable: S. Ostrach, Y. Kamotani (Case Western Reserve University), A. Pline (NASA GRC)
entries.fecha_periodo: June-July 1992 (STS-50) and PIV reanalysis in NASA PSI-108
entries.material_combustible: 10 cSt silicone fluid with 50-micron alumina tracers on flat and curved free surfaces
entries.condiciones: Surface thermal gradients of 5 to 60 °C; heating powers of 0.5 to 30 W; Marangoni number (Ma) up to 10^5 and high thermocapillary Reynolds number
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Quantify the velocity and structure of thermocapillary convection vortices (Marangoni effect) driven by surface-tension gradients without buoyant natural convection
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Thermocapillary flow fully dominates heat and mass transport in free-surface liquids in microgravity, controlling the preheating rate in liquid fuel pools, burning droplets and solder/melt pools
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Include Marangoni thermocapillary shear-stress boundary conditions (d_sigma/dT) in flame-spread models over liquids and molten polymer pools in microgravity.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-108

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-115: Advanced modelling of smoke generation (SAME data)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-115: Utilization of SAME Data for Advanced Modeling and Simulation of Smoke Generation in Microgravity
entries.categoria: Simulación numérica de balance poblacional y coagulación de aerosoles de humo en 0-g (Repositorio NASA PSI-115)
entries.instalacion_hardware: CFD-PBM (population balance modelling) coupled with experimental data from SAME (PSI-102) and SAME-R (PSI-101)
entries.investigador_responsable: NASA PSI-115 grant investigators / collaboration with the NASA GRC Smoke Detection Team
entries.material_combustible: Pyrolysis aerosols from Kapton, Teflon (PTFE), silicone rubber, cellulose and PMMA
entries.condiciones: General dynamic equation for aerosols (GDE) with homogeneous nucleation, condensation, fractal Brownian coagulation and thermophoretic deposition in a 1 to 7 cm/s duct
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Develop predictive tools for the generation and size evolution of smoke particles in microgravity using the SAME empirical database (PSI-102)
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: The model shows that the fractal dimension (Df ~ 1.7-1.9) and the lack of buoyant dilution at the source speed up the quadratic coagulation rate by 4x to 8x relative to 1 g, shifting the log-normal distribution toward larger diameters
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Integrate the aerosol population-balance module (PBM with fractal dimension 1.8) into habitat ventilation simulation software (Orion/Gateway) to optimize the placement of photoelectric detectors.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-115

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-117: Multiphysics CFD dynamics of cool flames under thermoconvective perturbation
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-117: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics: A Multiphysics Multidimensional CFD Analysis
entries.categoria: Análisis CFD 2D/3D de llamas frías en gotas y sprays bajo perturbaciones convectivas (Repositorio NASA PSI-117)
entries.instalacion_hardware: Multidimensional multiphysics CFD simulation validated with orbital data from FLEX (PSI-69) and counterflow (PSI-142)
entries.investigador_responsable: T. I. Farouk (U. South Carolina), F. L. Dryer, NASA PSI-117 grant investigators
entries.material_combustible: n-heptane, n-decane and dodecane droplets and aerosols under spray-relevant conditions
entries.condiciones: External convective velocity perturbations (0.5 to 25 cm/s) and thermal pulses; pressures of 1.0 to 3.0 atm; reduced skeletal kinetics with low-temperature chemistry (RO2 / QOOH)
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Determine how multidimensional asymmetries induced by external convective flows or droplet interaction change cool-flame stability and trigger hot reignition
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: A moderate convective perturbation accumulates intermediate species (peroxides and hydroperoxides) in the wake downstream of the droplet, which can cause an explosive secondary reignition to a hot flame, while an intense vortex breaks the NTC envelope and extinguishes the cool flame
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Avoid sudden ventilation pulses over post-extinction hydrocarbon vapour clouds, since the convective wake concentrates RO2/H2O2 radicals and triggers secondary hot reignition.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-117

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-142: Cool-flame transitions in radiative and strain extinction
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-142: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions in Radiative/Stretch Extinction using Counterflow Flames
entries.categoria: Cinética cuantitativa de transición llama caliente/fría en contracorriente y fluidos reactivos (Repositorio NASA PSI-142)
entries.investigador_responsable: Y. Ju (Princeton University), F. L. Dryer, NASA PSI-142 team
entries.material_combustible: Heavy alkanes (n-heptane, n-decane, n-dodecane) and esters in counterflow diffusion and premixed configurations
entries.condiciones: Aerodynamic strain rates of 5 to 300 1/s; controlled radiative losses; pressures of 1 to 3 atm
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Map the extended two-branch S-curve (hot flame and cool flame) to quantify the exact transition limits by radiation (low strain) and by aerodynamic strain (high strain)
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Established the unified four-branch S-curve flammability regimes, showing that the cool-flame branch survives strain rates and radiative losses at which the hot flame collapses
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Update strain-extinction criteria (critical Damköhler number) in space engines and suppression systems using the 4-branch S-curve that includes the cool-flame regime.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-142

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-159: ACME / CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-159: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (ACME CFI-G) in the ISS CIR
entries.categoria: Llamas frías de difusión puramente gaseosas en quemador esférico poroso (Repositorio NASA PSI-159)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / ACME porous spherical burner with intensified UV/visible cameras
entries.investigador_responsable: P. B. Sunderland (U. Maryland), R. L. Axelbaum (WUSTL), C. K. Law (Princeton), V. Nayagam (CWRU), D. L. Urban
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS operations 2021 / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-159
entries.material_combustible: Gaseous fuels: n-butane, propane and vaporized n-pentane diluted with N2 in an enriched atmosphere or air
entries.condiciones: Spherical burner with no liquid phase or free edge; pressures of 1.0 to 2.5 atm (101.3 to 253 kPa); O2 from 15% to 30%; long observation times (minutes)
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Achieve for the first time steady diffusion cool flames with purely gaseous fuels (no liquid droplets) in microgravity, to isolate gas-phase NTC chemistry from the liquid-vapour phase change
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Confirmed experimentally in the CIR that stable spherical cool flames of gaseous n-butane and n-pentane exist for several minutes, supporting the design of cleaner, more efficient HCCI/RCCI internal-combustion engines
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Extend cool-flame detection protocols (HCHO* and CO sensors) to leaks of light gaseous hydrocarbons (propane, butane, pentane) in space thermal and propulsion systems.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-159

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-181: Pb-Sn and Sn-Ag-Cu solders in microgravity and extreme temperatures (ISSI)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-181: Structure and Properties of Pb-Sn and Lead-Free Sn-Ag-Cu Solders in Terrestrial vs. Microgravity under Extreme Temperatures
entries.categoria: Confiabilidad termo-eléctrica de soldaduras espaciales, atrapamiento de poros y prevención de sobrecalentamiento/arcos (Repositorio NASA PSI-181)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG - In-Space Soldering Investigation ISSI PSI-77) + cryogenic/elevated thermal cycling on Earth
entries.investigador_responsable: R. N. Grugel (NASA MSFC), NASA PSI-181 grant investigators
entries.fecha_periodo: ISSI on the ISS (2004-2005) / PSI-181 microstructural and thermal study (2020-2023)
entries.material_combustible: Electronic solder alloys: eutectic Pb-Sn and lead-free Sn-Ag-Cu (SAC305) with organic Rosin flux
entries.condiciones: Manual soldering and reflow in microgravity; thermal cycling from cryogenic (-196 °C) to elevated (+150 °C) temperatures; analysis of porosity and Cu6Sn5 / Ag3Sn intermetallic phases
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Evaluate how the lack of buoyancy in microgravity traps flux vapour bubbles inside Pb-Sn and Sn-Ag-Cu solder joints, affecting electrical resistance, heat transfer and failure at extreme temperatures
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Joints soldered in microgravity retain large gas voids (porosity up to 5-10x higher than in 1 g), which reduces the effective electrical/thermal conduction section, creates Joule hot spots (risk of wire pyrolysis/ignition) and accelerates thermomechanical fracture under cryogenic cycling
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Use solder wire without a volatile flux core, or apply vacuum/ultrasonic degassing during in-orbit electronic repairs (in-space manufacturing/repair), to avoid trapped pores that create hot spots and electrical ignition; 2) Prefer doped SAC formulations with intermetallic control for lunar missions with cryogenic cycling.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-181 (derived from PSI-77)

entries.codigo_corto: LUCI & FM2: flammability at lunar gravity (0.16 g) and the U-shaped LOI curve
entries.experimento_investigacion: LUCI (Lunar-g Combustion Investigation) & FM2 (Flammability of Materials on the Moon) - Efecto Goldilocks y Escala de de Ris en 0.16g
entries.categoria: Inflamabilidad de sólidos en gravedad parcial lunar (0.16g), Curva LOI en U y Escala de de Ris
entries.instalacion_hardware: Centrífuga de caída libre NASA GRC / Cohete Sonda LUCI / Payload autónomo lunar CLPS FM2 / SoFIE (ISS MSG)
entries.investigador_responsable: S. L. Olson, P. V. Ferkul (NASA GRC), J. S. T'ien, Y.-T. Liao (Case Western Reserve University)
entries.material_combustible: Tejido SIBAL (algodón/fibra de vidrio), celulosa, películas delgadas y placas de PMMA, Nomex y Ultem
entries.condiciones: Gravedad lunar g = 0.16g (1.62 m/s2); velocidad boyante natural inducida Vb = (g*beta*dT*alpha)^(1/3) ~ 6.5-8.0 cm/s; presiones de 56.5 a 101.3 kPa; O2 de 13.5% a 34.0%
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Cuantificar el Índice Límite de Oxígeno (LOI en forma de U) y la velocidad de propagación de llama según la escala de de Ris en gravedad lunar (0.16g) frente a 0-g y 1-g
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Efecto 'Goldilocks' en la Luna (0.16g): en 1-g la fuerte flotabilidad (~20-30 cm/s) enfría y apaga la llama (blowoff), mientras en 0-g falta oxígeno sin ventilación; en cambio, en 0.16g la flotabilidad natural induce ~6.8-7.5 cm/s (justo en el mínimo de la curva LOI en U), haciendo que los materiales ardan a menor O2 en la Luna (LOI ~ 13.7-14.5% O2) que en la Tierra (LOI ~ 16.5-18.0% O2)
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Reemplazar la certificación terrestre NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (1-g) por ensayos o factores de corrección en el mínimo de la curva LOI en U (flujo equivalente de 6.5-8.0 cm/s para 0.16g lunar); 2) Incorporar en el motor de predicción la velocidad boyante intrínseca V_eff = sqrt(V_forced^2 + V_buoyant(g)^2) y la escala de de Ris (V_f ~ (k*rho*c)^(-1) para sólidos delgados).
entries.fuente: NASA GRC / NTRS & PSI - Olson, Ferkul, T'ien & Liao Partial-Gravity Flammability
entries.referencia: https://ntrs.nasa.gov / PSI SoFIE & BASS Partial-g Archive

entries.experimento_investigacion: SAFFIRE-IV, V, VI & SoFIE (GEL/MIST/SMuRF) in space exploration atmospheres (8.2 psia / 56.5 kPa and 34% O2)
entries.categoria: Incendios a gran escala y propagación en atmósferas de exploración Lunar Gateway / HLS / Marte (8.2 psia, 34% O2)
entries.instalacion_hardware: Northrop Grumman Cygnus vehicles (SAFFIRE-IV, V, VI with Far-Field Diagnostics FFD) and ISS MSG (SoFIE)
entries.investigador_responsable: G. A. Ruff, D. L. Urban, P. V. Ferkul, S. L. Olson (NASA GRC) / Exploration Atmospheres Working Group (EAWG)
entries.fecha_periodo: 2020-2024 (SAFFIRE IV-VI and SoFIE on the ISS) / NASA PSI & NTRS archive
entries.material_combustible: Flat and grooved PMMA panels, SIBAL fabric, silicone membranes, Nomex, Ultem and Delrin
entries.condiciones: Exploration atmosphere recommended by the NASA EAWG: reduced pressure of 8.2 psia (56.5 kPa) and 34% O2 (or 10.2 psia / 70.3 kPa and 26.5-32% O2) to eliminate pre-breathing before lunar/Martian EVAs
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Evaluate how the combination of high oxygen concentration (34% O2), low pressure (56.5 kPa) and partial gravity (0.16 g Moon / 0.38 g Mars) changes ignition, de Ris spread rate and the release of acid gases (CO, HCl, HF)
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: At 34% O2 and 56.5 kPa, fire-retardant materials that pass in standard air at 101.3 kPa (21% O2) sustain vigorous spread; the lower gas density reduces convective inertia, but the high O2 mole fraction raises the adiabatic flame temperature and speeds up de Ris heat transfer by a factor of 2.2x to 3.1x
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Prohibit materials certified only at 21% O2 inside modules pressurized to 8.2 psia / 34% O2 (HLS, Gateway, lunar/Martian rovers); 2) Install far-field catalytic scrubbers (Far-Field Scrubbers for CO, CO2, HCl and HF tested in SAFFIRE IV-VI) and a rapid post-fire depressurization/repressurization protocol.
entries.fuente: NASA PSI & NTRS - SAFFIRE-IV, V, VI & SoFIE Exploration Atmosphere Studies
entries.referencia: https://psi.nasa.gov / NASA EAWG 8.2 psia 34% O2 Technical Reports

entries.codigo_corto: MARS-0.38g & CO2-ISRU: combustion at Martian gravity and CO2 diluent
entries.experimento_investigacion: Inflamabilidad en Gravedad Marciana (0.38g), Efecto Supresor de Diluyente CO2 In-Situ y Seguridad de Oxígeno MOXIE/ISRU
entries.categoria: Combustión en gravedad marciana (0.38g), atmósfera diluida con CO2 y sistemas de producción de O2 In-Situ (ISRU/MOXIE)
entries.instalacion_hardware: Instalaciones de gravedad parcial NASA GRC / Quemadores con dilución CO2 (FLEX/ACME/SoFIE) / Arquitectura Mars ISRU (MOXIE)
entries.investigador_responsable: P. V. Ferkul, S. L. Olson, D. L. Dietrich (NASA GRC) & Equipo NASA Mars Architecture / ISRU
entries.fecha_periodo: 2018-2025 (Estudios de superficie marciana NASA NTRS / PSI)
entries.material_combustible: Polímeros de hábitat marciano (PMMA, telas compuestas, aislamientos) y líneas de alta presión de O2 de reactores Sabatier/MOXIE
entries.condiciones: Gravedad marciana g = 0.38g (3.72 m/s2); velocidad boyante natural Vb ~ 9.8-11.5 cm/s; atmósferas de hábitat (56.5-70.3 kPa, 26-34% O2) y uso de CO2 atmosférico marciano (95% CO2 exterior) como gas buffer o agente extintor
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Determinar el comportamiento de incendios en 0.38g (donde la velocidad boyante coincide con el pico de máxima velocidad de propagación de 10 cm/s) y cuantificar la eficacia del CO2 extraído de la atmósfera marciana como diluyente y supresor radiativo
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: En gravedad marciana (0.38g), el flujo boyante natural (~10.5 cm/s) cae exactamente en el régimen de máxima tasa de propagación de llama (pico de riesgo HVAC de 10 cm/s); sin embargo, sustituir parte del N2 por CO2 in-situ eleva el LOI en +2.5% a +3.8% O2 gracias a su alta capacidad calorífica molar y reabsorción radiativa en las bandas de 2.7 y 4.3 micras
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Aprovechar el CO2 atmosférico de Marte purificado e comprimido como sistema primario de inundación e inertización contra incendios en hábitats marcianos; 2) Aislar físicamente las plantas ISRU de electrólisis de óxido sólido (tipo MOXIE a 800 °C y alta pureza de O2) fuera del volumen habitable presurizado.
entries.fuente: NASA NTRS & PSI - Martian Partial-Gravity Combustion & CO2 Diluent Suppression
entries.referencia: https://ntrs.nasa.gov / PSI-68 & PSI-69 CO2 Diluent Archive

entries.codigo_corto: SAME/DAFT Lunar & Mars dust: telling regolith dust from smoke
entries.experimento_investigacion: Detección de Incendios Tolerante a Polvo Extraterrestre en Hábitats Lunares (0.16g) y Marcianos (0.38g) - Extensión SAME y DAFT
entries.categoria: Discriminación óptica multi-longitud de onda entre humo de pirólisis y polvo de regolito lunar/marciano (SAME / DAFT)
entries.instalacion_hardware: Sensores de dispersión láser multi-ángulo / multi-longitud de onda (Orion/Gateway Smoke Detector) + Datos SAME (PSI-101/102) y DAFT (PSI-47)
entries.investigador_responsable: D. L. Urban, G. A. Ruff, M. J. Meyer (NASA GRC) / NASA Lunar Dust & Smoke Detection Working Group
entries.fecha_periodo: 2018-2025 (Programa Artemis HLS / Lunar Gateway / Mars Transit)
entries.material_combustible: Humo de pirólisis de cables (Kapton, Teflón, silicona, CMD 0.09-0.9 um) mezclado con polvo de regolito lunar (silicatos vítreos abrasivos 0.5-20 um) y polvo marciano (óxidos de hierro y percloratos)
entries.condiciones: Sedimentación gravitacional lenta en la Luna (6x más lenta que en la Tierra, 0.16g) y Marte (2.6x más lenta, 0.38g) tras ingreso de trajes espaciales por esclusas EVA; presión 56.5-70.3 kPa
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Evitar falsas alarmas masivas provocadas por el polvo lunar y marciano en suspensión sin perder sensibilidad ante incendios incipientes o pirólisis de aislamientos eléctricos
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: En 0.16g y 0.38g el polvo fino (<5 micras) introducido tras cada caminata espacial permanece suspendido durante horas y dispara falsas alarmas en detectores ópticos simples; la firma de polarización y el cociente de dispersión entre láser azul (405 nm) e infrarrojo (880 nm) junto con sensores de gases (CO/HCN) permiten separar el regolito mineral facetado de las esférulas/agregados de humo
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Requerir detectores de humo multi-criterio (dispersión láser a dos longitudes de onda + despolarización óptica + celda electroquímica de CO) en todas las esclusas EVA y cabinas lunares/marcianas; 2) Activar modo de supresión de falsas alarmas por polvo sincronizado con la presurización de esclusas sin desactivar el canal de CO/pirólisis.
entries.fuente: NASA PSI-47 (DAFT), PSI-101/102 (SAME) & NTRS Lunar/Martian Dust-Tolerant Fire Detection

entries.codigo_corto: FLEX & CFI partial-g: cool flames and fuel droplets on the Moon and Mars
entries.experimento_investigacion: Transición de Llamas Frías (Cool Flames) y Reignición inducida por Pluma Boyante Débil en Gravedad Lunar (0.16g) y Marciana (0.38g)
entries.categoria: Combustión de gotas, sprays y química NTC de baja temperatura en gravedad parcial lunar y marciana
entries.instalacion_hardware: Modelado CFD Multifísico (PSI-117 / PSI-142) acoplado con datos de FLEX-2 (PSI-68), CFI (PSI-39) y CFI-G (PSI-159)
entries.investigador_responsable: T. I. Farouk, F. L. Dryer, D. L. Dietrich, V. Nayagam (NASA GRC)
entries.material_combustible: Hidrocarburos líquidos y gaseosos (n-heptano, n-decano, n-butano, metanol/etanol y propelentes verdes)
entries.condiciones: Gravedad lunar (0.16g, velocidad boyante ~4-7 cm/s alrededor de la gota) y marciana (0.38g, ~7-11 cm/s); presiones de 56.5 a 202.6 kPa
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Predecir si la convección natural débil de la Luna y Marte barre la nube de llama fría o si, por el contrario, concentra peróxidos RO2 en la estela superior provocando reignición explosiva
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Tal como demostró PSI-117 para flujos convectivos de 3-8 cm/s, la velocidad boyante propia de la gravedad lunar (0.16g) y marciana (0.38g) no es suficiente para soplar la llama fría (que requiere >20 cm/s), sino que estira la zona NTC en una pluma ascendente donde se acumulan hidroperóxidos y se dispara la reignición secundaria a llama caliente
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) En almacenes de solventes, laboratorios e invernaderos lunares/marcianos, mantener extracción forzada >25 cm/s o inertización con CO2/N2 tras cualquier conato líquido para impedir la reignición por pluma boyante de llama fría.
entries.fuente: NASA PSI-68, PSI-117 & PSI-159 Partial-Gravity Convective Cool Flame Analysis

entries.experimento_investigacion: Emulación Exacta de Flotabilidad Lunar (0.16g) y Marciana (0.38g) mediante Campo Eléctrico en Llamas Gaseosas (ACME E-FIELD PSI-22)
entries.categoria: Emulación electrohidrodinámica (EHD) de gravedad parcial lunar y marciana y control de hollín en quemadores Methalox (CH4/O2)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS CIR ACME E-FIELD (PSI-22), CLD Flame (PSI-21) y Flame Design (PSI-10)
entries.investigador_responsable: D. Dunn-Rankin (UC Irvine), R. L. Axelbaum (WUSTL), D. L. Urban (NASA GRC)
entries.material_combustible: Metano (CH4, propelente clave de aterrizadores lunares/marcianos Methalox) y etileno en aire y atmósferas enriquecidas en O2
entries.condiciones: Aplicación de campo eléctrico de 3.5-4.5 kV (fuerza cuerpo iónica equivalente a 0.16g lunar, V_ion ~ 6.8 cm/s) y 7.0-8.0 kV (equivalente a 0.38g marciano, V_ion ~ 10.4 cm/s) en el CIR de la ISS
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Utilizar la fuerza de Coulomb sobre los iones quimio-ionizados de la llama en 0-g para reproducir de manera estacionaria la convección boyante de la Luna y Marte y controlar el punto de humo
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: El viento iónico permite reproducir en la ISS la estructura exacta de llamas lunares (0.16g) y marcianas (0.38g) durante minutos (superando los 2-5 s de las torres de caída), demostrando que en 0.16g y 0.38g la emisión de hollín sigue siendo 2x mayor que en 1-g a menos que se aplique control eléctrico o diseño estequiométrico Z_st
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Emplear la correlación voltaje-gravedad de PSI-22 (E-FIELD) para calificar quemadores, antorchas de procesamiento de regolito y sensores de fugas de metano (CH4/LOX) para misiones lunares y marcianas.

entries.experimento_investigacion: Dinámica de Sedimentación y Extinción por Niebla Fina de Agua (Fine Water Mist) en Hábitats Lunares (0.16g) y Marcianos (0.38g)
entries.categoria: Extinción de incendios mediante niebla fina de agua (Water Mist) y sistemas híbridos N2/CO2 en gravedad parcial
entries.instalacion_hardware: Portable Fire Extinguisher (PFE) de Niebla Fina de Agua de la ISS + Cámaras de supresión para Lunar Gateway y Hábitats de Marte
entries.investigador_responsable: A. Abbud-Madrid, J. T. McKinnon (Colorado School of Mines), F. Takahashi (NASA GRC)
entries.fecha_periodo: 2016-2025 (Estudios de supresión para Artemis Gateway, HLS y Marte)
entries.material_combustible: Incendios de polímeros de cabina, racks electrónicos y baterías de iones de litio bajo atmósferas de exploración (56.5-70.3 kPa, 26-34% O2)
entries.condiciones: Gotas de agua de 10-30 micras en gravedad lunar (0.16g, velocidad terminal de caída 6.2x menor que en la Tierra) y marciana (0.38g, 2.6x menor)
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Optimizar el diámetro de gota y la velocidad de descarga de los extintores de niebla de agua para aprovechar la baja velocidad de sedimentación en la Luna y Marte sin provocar intensificación inicial por arrastre de O2
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: En 0.16g y 0.38g las gotas de niebla fina (15-25 micras) permanecen suspendidas mucho más tiempo que en 1-g, comportándose casi como un gas total-flooding que penetra detrás de los racks y absorbe calor latente; en atmósferas de 34% O2, combinar niebla fina de agua con CO2/N2 evita el fortalecimiento inicial de la llama
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Estandarizar extintores híbridos de niebla fina de agua (D32 < 25 micras) + gas inerte (N2 en la Luna, CO2 in-situ en Marte) para hábitats de superficie a 56.5-70.3 kPa.

entries.experimento_investigacion: Confiabilidad de Soldaduras Electrónicas (Pb-Sn y SAC305) y Prevención de Ignición por Arco bajo Gravedad Parcial y Noche Lunar (-196 °C)
entries.categoria: Manufactura y reparación en el espacio (ISM), porosidad de soldadura en 0.16g/0.38g y fatiga criogénica lunar/marciana
entries.instalacion_hardware: Investigación ISSI (PSI-181 / PSI-77) aplicada a mantenimiento autónomo en Lunar Gateway, HLS y superficie de la Luna/Marte
entries.investigador_responsable: R. N. Grugel (NASA MSFC) & Equipo de Confiabilidad Electrónica NASA PSI-181
entries.material_combustible: Uniones soldadas Pb-Sn y Sn-Ag-Cu (SAC305) en tarjetas de potencia expuestas a 34% O2 (56.5 kPa) y ciclado térmico lunar (-196 °C a +125 °C)
entries.condiciones: Empuje de Arquímedes reducido en 0.16g (Luna) y 0.38g (Marte) durante reflujo de soldadura + fatiga extrema durante los 14 días de noche lunar criogénica
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Cuantificar la retención de burbujas de vapor de fundente en gravedad lunar/marciana y prevenir fracturas intermetálicas que generen puntos calientes Joule o micro-arcos en atmósferas enriquecidas al 34% O2
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: En 0.16g la fuerza boyante sigue siendo 6 veces menor que en la Tierra, atrapando hasta un 12-15% de porosidad si se usa fundente convencional; al combinarse con el ciclado térmico de la noche lunar (-196 °C) y una atmósfera de cabina de 34% O2, un punto caliente o micro-arco en una unión porosa enciende el aislamiento adyacente en menos de 2 segundos

entries.experimento_investigacion: SoFIE — 5 official sub-projects in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) up to 37% O2 (8.2 psia SEA)
entries.categoria: Inflamabilidad de combustibles sólidos en microgravedad y atmósferas de exploración Artemis SEA (34-37% O2)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) — GEL, MIST, SMuRF, RTDFS and NCA modules
entries.investigador_responsable: J.S. T'ien (GEL), C. Fernandez-Pello (MIST), S. Olson (SMuRF), S. Bhattacharjee (RTDFS), F. Miller (NCA) — NASA GRC
entries.material_combustible: PMMA spheres and cylinders, thin sheets, a thick plate in a narrow channel and real spacecraft materials
entries.condiciones: 8.2 psia (56.5 kPa) with a control band up to 37% O2 (and CIR mixtures up to 85% O2 / 15% N2) + external radiant heater (MIST)
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Close the gap between 1 g ground tests (NASA-STD-6001B Test 1) and the real behaviour of spacecraft materials in microgravity and lunar/Martian atmospheres

entries.experimento_investigacion: Standards: NASA-STD-6001B Test 1 (15.2 cm), JSC 20584 SMACs and NASA-STD-3001 dust/perchlorates
entries.categoria: Certificación de materiales, toxicología post-incendio (HCl, HF, CO) y control de polvo lunar/marciano
entries.instalacion_hardware: SAFFIRE IV-VI Far-Field Diagnostics (FFD), Smoke Eater, CO2/acid scrubber and HEPA filtration for Artemis/Mars
entries.investigador_responsable: NASA Technical Standards & JSC Toxicology and Environmental Chemistry Lab
entries.material_combustible: Non-metallic cabin materials + post-fire acid gases (HCl, HF, CO, HCN) + lunar dust (~0.1 mg/m3) and Martian perchlorates
entries.condiciones: Vertical Test 1 (self-extinguishes < 15.2 cm / 6 in with no burning drips), 1 h/24 h/long-term SMACs (HF = 0.3 ppm) and additive index T_grp = sum(Ci/SMACi) < 1

lunar_mars_physics_and_de_ris_scaling.description: Parámetros físicos de gravedad parcial Lunar (0.16g) y Marciana (0.38g), curva LOI en forma de U (Olson-Ferkul-T'ien) y escala de propagación de de Ris integrados con el modelo ONNX

moon_lunar_0.16g.goldilocks_hazard_note: En 0.16g la flotabilidad natural (~6.8 cm/s) sitúa la llama exactamente en el mínimo de la curva LOI en U (13.7% O2), haciendo que los materiales ardan más fácilmente en la Luna que en la Tierra (1-g).

mars_martian_0.38g.mars_hazard_note: En 0.38g la velocidad boyante (~10.4 cm/s) coincide con el pico de máxima velocidad de propagación de llama (10 cm/s); usar CO2 marciano in-situ eleva el LOI en +3.2% O2 por absorción radiativa.

u_shaped_loi_and_de_ris_equations.buoyant_velocity_formula: V_b(g) = V_b_1g * (g / 1.0)**(1/3), con V_b_1g ~ 12.5 a 25.0 cm/s; V_eff = sqrt(V_forced**2 + V_b(g)**2)
u_shaped_loi_and_de_ris_equations.u_curve_loi_formula: LOI(V_eff, P) = LOI_min + k_rad / (V_eff + 0.5) + k_blow * (V_eff - V_opt)**2 * (101.3 / P)**0.35
